entries.body: Mom took me and Lucas to the park after school. Some leaves are turning yellow already. Lucas found a yellow one and said it is gold. He gave it to mom. Then he found like a hundred more and threw them in the air. I pushed Lucas on the swing. He says higher higher but I don't push too high because he is only three. Then I went on the big kid swing and pumped my legs by myself.
entries.highlight: Played at the park with Lucas and noticed the first leaves turning yellow.

entries.title: Frisbee at recess
entries.body: I brought my frisbee to school for recess. Mr. Okafor said okay but be careful. Me and Theo and Sofia played. Sofia did not know how to throw it, so I showed her like dad showed me. Flick your wrist. She got it on the third try. Then I tried to catch it behind my back and it actually worked one time! Theo said no way. I said it was like a sea lion doing a trick at the aquarium. Then the frisbee went on the roof of the shed and the recess teacher had to get it with a stick.
entries.highlight: Brought a frisbee to recess and taught some classmates to throw it.

entries.title: New swim level at the indoor pool
entries.body: Swim lessons started again at the indoor pool. I am in level two now! I got a little card that says it. Miss Marina is not my teacher this time. My new teacher is Coach Ray. He is really loud but in a nice way. We learned freestyle arms. You reach and pull like you are climbing a ladder in the water. And you turn your head to breathe. I swallowed some water. It tasted like a swimming pool, which makes sense.
entries.highlight: Moved up to level two swim lessons at the indoor pool and learned freestyle arms.

entries.title: So hungry after swimming
entries.body: After swim lessons I was so hungry. Swimming makes you so hungry. Coach Ray said that is because you used all your muscles. Mom got me a big soft pretzel at the snack window. It was as big as my face. I ate the whole thing and then I ate a banana in the car and then some crackers at home. Mom said are you a bottomless pit? I said yes. Lucas said he is a bottomless pit too.
entries.highlight: Felt extra hungry after swim lessons and ate a big soft pretzel.

entries.title: Sprinkler in September
entries.body: It was so hot today even though it is September. After I did my homework, mom said sprinkler time. My homework was adding with two numbers. I got them all right. Then I put on my swim trunks and ran through the sprinkler with Lucas. I did my freestyle arms in the air. Lucas said what are you doing? I said swimming. He did it too. We were swimming on the grass.
entries.highlight: Ran through the sprinkler after homework on an unusually hot September day.

entries.title: Washing Lucas's trike
entries.body: Lucas's tricycle was so muddy from the puddle. He was sad because it was dirty. So I said let's give it a car wash. Like me and dad do. I got the hose and Lucas got a sponge. I showed him to wash from the top down. He got so much soap on it. Then I sprayed it clean. Lucas said it is shiny again! He rode it in a circle and rang the bell like a hundred times.
entries.highlight: Helped Lucas wash his muddy tricycle with the hose and a sponge.

entries.title: I made a Laser chart
entries.body: I made a chart for Laser so I never forget again. It has every day of the week. And it has two boxes for each day. Food and water. When I do it I put a sticker. Mom gave me star stickers. I hung it on the fridge right next to Laser's bowl, so I see it every morning. Today I put two stars. Mom said this is a very grown up idea. I said it is because my brain forgets when I am excited. Now the chart remembers for me.
entries.highlight: Made a feeding chart with stickers so he would never forget Laser's food and water again.

entries.title: Ruby and the cat cave
entries.body: Ruby came over and we built a big blanket tent in my room. This time we made a little cave inside it just for Laser. We put a soft towel in it. Ruby said cats like small spaces because they feel safe. Laser came in and smelled everything and then she went in the cave and curled up! It worked! I showed Ruby my Laser chart. She said that is smart. She is going to make one for her goldfish.
entries.highlight: Built a blanket tent with Ruby with a special small cave just for Laser.

entries.title: Apple orchard with mom
entries.body: Mom and me went to the apple orchard. Dad stayed home with Lucas because he had a cold. We got a bag and picked red apples and yellow apples. I had to climb a little ladder to get the high ones. I found one almost as big as my head. Mom took a picture of me with it. Then we got apple cider donuts. They had sugar all over them. I saved half of mine for Lucas because he was sick.
entries.highlight: Went apple picking with mom and found an apple almost as big as his head.

entries.title: Sofia draws on the clubhouse walls
entries.body: Sofia came over in the afternoon. We made a clubhouse out of the big box from our new chair. Sofia brought markers and we drew on the walls. She drew Laser and it looked so real. I drew a submarine and a whale. Sofia said my whale looks like a potato. I said it is a potato whale. Then she laughed so hard. We put a sign on the door that says no grown ups.
entries.highlight: Built a cardboard clubhouse with Sofia and decorated the walls with drawings.

entries.title: Puppy class at the park
entries.body: At the park there was a puppy class! Like school for puppies. There were six puppies and their owners. The teacher said sit and the puppies sat. Well, most of them. One puppy just rolled over. I watched the whole time. The teacher gave treats right away, just like I did with Laser. I told mom I already know how to train a puppy. Mom smiled and said I know you do.
entries.highlight: Watched a puppy training class at the park and paid attention to how they learned.

entries.title: Mr. Okafor reads a chapter book
entries.body: At story time Mr. Okafor is reading us a chapter book. It does not have a lot of pictures. It has chapters and you read one a day. It is about a kid who lives in a lighthouse. Every chapter ends at the most exciting part. Today the kid heard a noise in the fog and then Mr. Okafor said, to be continued. Everybody groaned. I want to know what the noise was. I think it was a whale. Did you know whale songs can go for miles under the water? Maybe I can read chapter books someday. Maybe one about sharks.
entries.highlight: Listened to Mr. Okafor read a chapter book aloud and could not wait for the next chapter.

entries.title: Trading snacks at lunch
entries.body: At lunch everybody trades snacks. It is like a store. Theo had cheese puffs and I had pretzels so we traded. Then Noah had seaweed snacks. Seaweed! Like sea turtles eat! Did you know there is a shark that eats seaweed too? It is called a bonnethead. I said can I try one. It was crunchy and salty and kind of like paper. I liked it! Noah said most people say yuck. I said I am an ocean person. Ruby traded me two mango slices for my cookie. Mango is still my favorite trade.
entries.highlight: Traded snacks with friends at lunch and finally tried a seaweed snack.

entries.title: Movie night with a lighthouse movie
entries.body: We had movie night and I got to pick. I picked a movie with a lighthouse in it because of our book at school. It was a little bit boring in the middle. But the ending had a big storm and the lighthouse saved a boat. Lucas fell asleep on my arm. My arm fell asleep too. It got all tingly. I did not move because he looked so comfy. Mom took a picture of us.
entries.highlight: Picked a movie about a lighthouse for family movie night because of the class book.

entries.title: Show and tell with my Laser chart
entries.body: Today was show and tell. Most kids brought toys. I brought my Laser chart and a picture of Laser in her box. I told the class how I forgot to feed her and then I made the chart so I do not forget. Mr. Okafor said that is called problem solving. Everybody wanted to know about Laser. Sofia asked if Laser can do tricks. I said she can high five. Everybody said whoa. I want to bring Laser for real but cats are not allowed.
entries.highlight: Brought his Laser feeding chart and a photo of Laser to show and tell.

entries.title: Lucas finally caught the frisbee
entries.body: I took Lucas to play frisbee in the front yard while dad watched. I threw it really soft and really slow. Lucas missed like ten times. He got kind of sad. I said keep your hands like a sandwich. And then I threw one more and he caught it! With his hands and his tummy at the same time. He screamed I DID IT. I was so happy for him. Last summer he threw it backwards and hit dad. Now he can catch.
entries.favorite: Lucas catching it with his tummy
entries.highlight: Played frisbee with Lucas at the park and cheered when Lucas finally caught one.

entries.title: Noah and the giant leaf pile
entries.body: Me and Noah went to the park after school. The leaves are falling for real now. We used our hands and our feet to make a giant pile under the big tree. It was so tall, almost up to my belly. Then we counted to three and jumped in. Crunch! It was like jumping in the pool, but crunchy. Leaves went in my shirt and my hair and my shoes. Noah found a worm in the pile. He named it Steve. We put Steve back in the dirt.
entries.highlight: Made a giant leaf pile with Noah at the park and jumped in it over and over.

entries.title: Apple pie with the orchard apples
entries.body: Dad and me made apple pie with the apples from the orchard. I washed them and dad peeled them. Then I put cinnamon and sugar on them and mixed it with my hands. It was so sticky. Dad let me roll out the dough. It had holes in it but dad said that is how air gets in. That is not true I think. We made a little leaf on the top. Laser sat on a chair and watched like she was the boss of the pie. The whole house smelled like grandma's house. It was so good warm.
entries.highlight: Baked an apple pie with dad using the apples from the orchard trip.

entries.title: A kind of spooky movie
entries.body: Tonight we watched a Halloween movie. It was spooky but not too scary. There was a friendly ghost and a pumpkin that could talk. Lucas got scared when the lights went out in the movie. So I told him it is just pretend. They are actors. I held his hand and he held mom's hand. I was a little scared too. But I did not tell Lucas. A big brother has to be brave.
entries.highlight: Watched a spooky Halloween movie with the family and helped Lucas not be scared.

entries.title: Ruby's goldfish chart
entries.body: Ruby came over after school and we built a cave with the couch cushions. She brought something to show me. It was her goldfish chart! It is just like my Laser chart but it has goldfish stickers. She said it was my idea. I felt so proud that my idea helped somebody. Then in the cave we made a list of all the animals we want someday. Mine was a puppy, a turtle and a shark. Ruby said you can't have a shark. I said a little one.
entries.highlight: Built a couch cushion cave with Ruby, who showed him the feeding chart she made for her goldfish.

entries.title: Saving a ladybug from Laser
entries.body: Laser found a ladybug on the window. She was tapping it with her paw. I said Laser no! The ladybug is little and it can't fight back. I got a piece of paper and let the ladybug crawl on it. It tickled. Then I took it outside and put it on the bush. Laser was mad at me. She gave me a look. I gave her a treat so she would not be mad. Ruby says ladybugs eat the bugs that hurt plants.
entries.highlight: Rescued a ladybug from Laser and carried it safely outside.

entries.title: The thousand piece puzzle
entries.body: Family game night was a puzzle this time. It is an ocean puzzle with a thousand pieces. It has a coral reef on it. Did you know coral is made of tiny animals? Dad said no way and then he looked it up. A thousand! That is like ten hundreds. Dad said we do the edges first. I found all four corners. Lucas found a piece and said this one and put it in his pocket. We did not finish. We will do more tomorrow. Mom said nobody bump the table. Especially not Laser. Laser is already looking at it.
entries.highlight: Started a giant ocean jigsaw puzzle during family game night.

entries.title: Making caramel apples
entries.body: After school mom and me made caramel apples. You put a stick in the apple and dip it in the hot caramel. Mom did the dipping part because it is hot. Then I rolled mine in nuts and Lucas rolled his in sprinkles. We put them on wax paper to get hard. My caramel slid down to the bottom like a skirt. When I bit it, it was so sticky my teeth almost got stuck together. But so good.
entries.highlight: Made caramel apples with mom and rolled his in chopped nuts.

entries.title: Laser and the rain
entries.body: It rained all day so I stayed inside. Laser was on the windowsill watching the rain. Every time a drop hit the window she tapped it with her paw. Then she got sleepy and fell asleep right there. I sat next to her and read a book about sharks. I could hear her purring. It is like a little motor. Mom said rainy days are for cats and books. That is true.
entries.highlight: Watched rain with sleepy Laser on the windowsill on a gray Saturday.

entries.title: Carving pumpkins
entries.body: We carved pumpkins today. First you scoop out the guts. They are slimy and cold and stringy. I did not like it at first but then it was fun. Lucas would not touch them. He said ewww. I carved a shark face with teeth. Dad helped with the knife. Lucas drew a face and mom carved it for him. It looks so surprised. We saved the seeds and dad roasted them with salt.
entries.highlight: Carved jack-o-lanterns with the family and made a shark pumpkin.

entries.title: Trying to draw Laser
entries.body: After pumpkins I tried to draw Laser. She was sitting very still on the chair like she was posing. I drew a circle for her head and a bigger circle for her body. But then her ears looked like a bat. And her legs looked like a table. Cats are hard to draw! The tail was the best part. I made it all curly. I showed mom and she said it is beautiful. Moms always say that. I will try again.
entries.highlight: Tried to draw Laser while she sat still, and found cats are hard to draw.

entries.title: Showing mom my chart for puppy reasons
entries.body: I asked mom for a puppy again. But this time I had proof. I showed her my Laser chart. Every box has a star. Five weeks of stars. I said see, I am responsible now. Mom looked at it for a long time. She said this is really impressive. She said a puppy is a lot more work than a cat. They need walks every day, even in the rain and snow. I said I can do it. She said we will see. But it was a nicer we will see.
entries.highlight: Showed mom that his Laser chart had all stars as proof he could handle a puppy.

entries.title: Laser said no to the costume
entries.body: Tomorrow is Halloween so I tried to put a little witch hat on Laser. It was from my old toy. She wore it for one second. Then she shook her head and the hat flew off. And then she ran under the bed and would not come out. I said sorry Laser. Mom said cats do not like costumes. Some cats are okay but not Laser. I put the hat on Practice Waffles instead. He does not care.
entries.favorite: Laser wearing the hat for one second
entries.highlight: Tried to put a tiny witch hat on Laser for Halloween, and she escaped.

entries.title: Halloween as a scuba diver
entries.body: I dressed up as a scuba diver for Halloween! I had my swim goggles and a snorkel and two soda bottles painted silver on my back for air tanks. Lucas was a clownfish. Did you know all clownfish start out as boys? I told Lucas and he said he is still a boy clownfish. Mom made his costume orange and white. We went trick-or-treating together. I held his hand at the doors with the scary decorations. One house had a fog machine. Lucas was scared, so I went first. We got like a zillion pieces of candy and my bag was heavy.
entries.highlight: Dressed as a scuba diver for Halloween and went trick-or-treating with Lucas the clownfish.

entries.title: Sorting all my candy
entries.body: After trick-or-treating I dumped my candy on the floor. I sorted it into piles. Chocolate, gummy, lollipops, and yucky ones. I had sixty-three pieces! One house gave a full size chocolate bar. That is the best house. Lucas does not know how to sort so I helped him. He has a lot of raisins. I traded him one gummy worm for two chocolates. He said okay. Mom said only two pieces tonight. I picked a gummy worm and the chocolate bar.
entries.highlight: Sorted and counted his Halloween candy into piles on the living room floor.

entries.title: Library card day with mom
entries.body: Mom took me to the library and I got my very own library card! I had to sign my name on the back. I did it in my best writing. Then I could pick out books on my card. I picked six! Four about the ocean, one joke book for Kai, and one about a dog who goes to space. The librarian scanned them with my card. Beep. I felt so grown up. I read one in the car on the way home.
entries.favorite: Signing my name on the card
entries.highlight: Got his very own library card on a trip with mom and checked out six books.

entries.title: Shark tag at recess
entries.body: I made up a game at recess. It is called shark tag. One person is the shark and everybody else is a minnow. If the shark tags you, you become a shark too. At the end there is only one minnow. Theo and Sofia and Noah played. Then more kids came. Like the whole class! Mr. Okafor said it was the best organized game he has seen. Sofia was the last minnow. She is so fast.
entries.highlight: Made up a game of shark tag at recess that the whole class wanted to play.

entries.title: Reading the joke book to Kai
entries.body: Kai came over and I read him the joke book from the library. Why do sharks swim in salt water? Because pepper water makes them sneeze. Kai did not get it at first. Then he laughed so hard. Then I read why did the cookie go to the doctor? Because it felt crummy. Kai was drinking milk and he snorted. Some came out his nose. That was the funniest thing that happened all week. Now Kai wants to make his own joke book.
entries.highlight: Read jokes from his library book to Kai and they laughed until Kai snorted.

entries.title: Drawing Laser again
entries.body: I tried to draw Laser again. This time I looked at her ears really carefully first. They are triangles, but a little bit curvy. Last time they looked like bat ears. This time they look like cat ears! Her legs are still kind of weird. Mom said artists practice the same thing many times. So I will do it again. Laser was sleeping so she did not move. That helps. Sleeping cats are easier to draw.
entries.favorite: Laser's ears looking like cat ears
entries.highlight: Tried drawing Laser again and her ears came out much better this time.

entries.title: Laser and the stink bug
entries.body: Laser found a stink bug on the floor today. She batted it around. Then she sniffed it really close. And then she made the funniest face. Her mouth opened and her nose went all crinkly. Dad said that is the stink. I laughed so hard. Dad put the bug outside. Laser walked away like she did not care. But I saw her wash her face for a long time.
entries.highlight: Watched Laser catch a stink bug and make a disgusted face.

entries.title: Chicken soup for Lucas
entries.body: Lucas was sick today with a fever. So after school me and dad made chicken soup. Dad let me cut the carrots with the kid knife. I made them into little circles like coins. Then we put in the noodles at the end. Dad said soup helps when you are sick because it is warm. I brought a bowl to Lucas on the couch. He ate four spoons. He said thank you Matty. I hope he feels better tomorrow.
entries.highlight: Helped dad make chicken noodle soup when Lucas was home sick.

entries.title: We finished the ocean puzzle
entries.body: We finished the ocean puzzle! It took a whole month. Every game night we did a little more. Tonight there were only like twenty pieces left. And then there was one hole and no more pieces. Everybody looked. Then Lucas said oh and took a piece out of his pajama pocket. He had it the whole time! He let me put it in. Dad took a picture. Mom said we should glue it and put it on the wall.
entries.highlight: Finished the thousand-piece ocean puzzle at family game night and put in the last piece.

entries.title: I moved up a reading group
entries.body: Mr. Okafor told me I am moving up to a new reading group! It is called the dolphins. Did you know dolphins have names for each other? They whistle them. The books are longer and the words are harder. My first book in the new group is about a girl and a robot. It has some chapters but they are short. I read the first one by myself at quiet time. Mr. Okafor said all that reading at home is paying off. I think it was the library card. I told mom at pick up and she squeezed me.
entries.highlight: Moved up to a harder reading group in second grade and felt proud.

entries.title: Popcorn and the movie snack mix
entries.body: Mom let me make snack mix for Friday night. I put popcorn, pretzels, cereal and little chocolate candies in a big bowl and shook it up. Then I picked out all the chocolate candies first. Mom said that is not how snack mix works. Lucas picked out only the pretzels. So the popcorn was left for mom and dad. Laser tried to steal a popcorn and carried it away. She never eats it. She just likes to steal it.
entries.favorite: Finding the chocolate candies in the mix
entries.highlight: Made a big bowl of snack mix for movie night and searched for the chocolate pieces.

entries.title: Two whole months of stars
entries.body: Today I finished two whole months on my Laser chart. Every single box has a star. I never forgot one time! Dad wrote a note on the bottom. It says Matthew can be trusted. I read it like ten times. Mom said that means a lot. I remember when I forgot Laser's breakfast and she cried by her bowl. That felt so bad. Now Laser never has to cry. I think this is good puppy practice.
entries.highlight: Filled two whole months of his Laser chart without forgetting and felt trusted.

entries.title: Car wash before grandma's
entries.body: Dad and me went to the car wash so the car is clean for driving to grandma's. Lucas came too. He was scared of the big brushes. He said the monsters are eating the car. I held his hand. I said they are just brushes, look, they are blue and fluffy. Like big muppets. Then he laughed. I used to think it was like a dishwasher. Now I think it is like a muppet party. Lucas wants to go again.
entries.favorite: Lucas holding my hand in the car wash
entries.highlight: Took the car through the car wash with dad before the Thanksgiving drive and helped Lucas not be scared.

entries.title: Thanksgiving with two green beans
entries.body: We went to grandma's for Thanksgiving. Grandma made turkey and stuffing and her pumpkin pie and an apple pie too. Grandma has a new pie rule. Now that I am seven you have to eat two green beans. I ate three to be safe. At the table I said I am thankful for my family and Laser and for learning to swim in the deep end. Grandma said that is a lot to be thankful for. Lucas said he is thankful for pie.
entries.highlight: Celebrated Thanksgiving at grandma's and said he was thankful for Laser and learning to swim.

entries.title: Laser in the pie box
entries.body: When we got home from grandma's we had leftover pie in a big box. Mom put the pie in the fridge and the box on the floor. Laser jumped right in! She sniffed all the corners because it smelled like pumpkin. Then she curled up and fell asleep. I gave her extra food because she was alone all day. I checked my chart and it was already done, but I gave a little extra anyway. It is Thanksgiving for cats too.
entries.highlight: Came home from grandma's and found Laser curled up in the empty pie box.

entries.title: Throwing a football with Theo
entries.body: Me and Theo went to the park with his new football. Footballs are hard to throw. They wobble like a duck. Theo showed me how to hold it on the laces. My throw went kind of straight! Then Theo threw a long one and I ran and caught it. I fell in the grass but I held on. Theo said touchdown! We did a dance. Theo still likes the great white best. I still like hammerheads.
entries.highlight: Practiced throwing a football with Theo at the park after Thanksgiving.

entries.title: Picking the Christmas tree with mom
entries.body: Mom and me picked out the Christmas tree. Dad stayed home because Lucas had a nap. At the tree place there were like a hundred trees. We walked up and down. Some were too short and some were too skinny. I found one that was really tall and really fat. Mom said too big for the door. Then we found one that was just right. The man tied it on the car. Mom said I have a good tree eye.
entries.highlight: Helped mom pick out the Christmas tree at the tree lot.

entries.title: Lucas had a bad dream
entries.body: Last night Lucas had a bad dream. He came into my room crying. He said there was a monster in his closet. I did not get mad even though it was the middle of the night. I took my flashlight and we went to his room and checked the closet. Only clothes. I told him monsters are scared of big brothers. I sat on his bed until he fell asleep. He held my hand. In the morning he said Matty saved me.
entries.favorite: Lucas falling asleep holding my hand
entries.highlight: Comforted Lucas after he woke up from a bad dream and stayed until he fell asleep.

entries.title: Christmas movie and the tree lights
entries.body: We had movie night with only the Christmas tree lights on. It was so cozy. We watched the one with the grumpy green guy who steals Christmas. His heart grows three sizes at the end. I like that part. Lucas sat on my lap. Laser climbed into the tree skirt and fell asleep under the tree like a present. Mom said she is our cat present. Dad said that is the only present that sheds.
entries.favorite: The tree lights in the dark
entries.highlight: Watched a Christmas movie with only the Christmas tree lights on.

entries.title: Gingerbread house with Noah
entries.body: Noah came over and we made a gingerbread house. The walls kept falling down. Mom said the frosting is the glue. We held the walls for like five minutes. Then it stayed! We put gumdrops on the roof and candy canes by the door. I made a blue frosting pool in the backyard with a gummy shark in it. Noah made a frosting snowman in the yard. I ate some gumdrops. Okay, like eight. Noah ate some too. The house has fewer gumdrops now. But it still looks good.
entries.highlight: Built a gingerbread house with Noah during a playdate and ate some of the decorations.

entries.title: Snow recess
entries.body: It snowed last night so recess was in the snow! Mr. Okafor made sure we all had boots and mittens. Me and Theo and Noah built a snow wall. Then other kids helped and it got really long. I named it the Great Barrier Wall, like the reef. Did you know the Great Barrier Reef is so big you can see it from space? Sofia made snowballs and stacked them like a pyramid. Mr. Okafor said no throwing snowballs at faces, only at the wall. My mittens got soaked. We put them on the heater in the classroom to dry. The room smelled like wet socks.
entries.favorite: Building the long snow wall with the class
entries.highlight: Played in the first real snow at recess and built a snow wall with classmates.

entries.title: Snow ice cream
entries.body: Mom said we can make snow ice cream. You go outside and get a big bowl of clean snow. Not yellow snow! Then you put milk and sugar and vanilla and stir. It turns into ice cream. Kind of. It is crunchy and cold and sweet. Lucas wanted to eat snow off the porch. I said not that snow, it has boot prints. We ate it fast because it melts. Mom said only on snow days.
entries.highlight: Made snow ice cream with mom using fresh clean snow, milk and sugar.

entries.title: The movie theater on winter break
entries.body: It was the first day of winter break so we went to the movie theater. We saw a cartoon about a whale who wants to find his family. The screen is so big. I could see the whale's eye so close. Did you know a blue whale heart is as big as a little car? I told dad in a whisper. Lucas sat on the seat that folds and it almost folded him up. Dad caught him. Me and dad shared a popcorn bucket with like a million pieces in it. At the sad part I almost cried but I did not. Mom cried a little. She always cries at movies.
entries.highlight: Went to the movie theater on winter break and saw an animated ocean adventure.

entries.title: Burgers at the diner with grandma
entries.body: Grandma took me and Lucas to the diner. It has red seats that squeak. I got a hamburger and french fries. I dipped my fries in the milkshake like dad showed me. Grandma said that is disgusting and then she tried it. She liked it! Lucas and I shared a chocolate milkshake with two straws. He drinks so fast. I said Lucas, sharing means half. He drank slower after. Grandma left a big tip and the waitress gave us candy canes.
entries.highlight: Ate burgers and fries at the diner with grandma and shared a milkshake with Lucas.

entries.title: Christmas and the dog detective books
entries.body: It was Christmas and it snowed again, just like last year. I woke up at six but mom said wait until six thirty. That was the longest thirty minutes ever. I got a snorkel and a set of chapter books about a dog who is a detective. There are four books! Real chapter books, with only a few pictures. Lucas got a big green dinosaur that roars when you squeeze it. He squeezed it like a hundred times. Laser got a cat tree from Santa and she sat in the box it came in instead. Of course.
entries.highlight: Got a set of dog detective chapter books for Christmas, and Lucas got a dinosaur.

entries.title: Taking Lucas down the big hill
entries.body: After presents we went sledding. Last year Lucas only went on the little hill. This year he wanted to go on the big hill with me. Mom said only if Matthew holds on to you. So I sat in the back and Lucas sat in the front and I held him with both arms. We went so fast and the snow sprayed in our faces. At the bottom Lucas yelled again again! We went like ten times. My legs were so tired from walking up. But I did not mind because he was so happy.
entries.highlight: Went sledding after Christmas presents and took Lucas down the big hill for the first time.

entries.title: Grandma's mystery game
entries.body: Grandma came over for game night. We played a mystery game where you have to guess who did it, in which room, with what thing. I had to read the cards and keep a secret list. I figured out it was the professor in the kitchen with the rope! Dad was so close but he guessed the library. Grandma said I have a detective brain. I think it is from my dog detective book. I only read one chapter so far but it is already helping.
entries.highlight: Played a mystery board game at family game night and solved it before dad.

entries.title: Shark Bite for the new year
entries.body: On the last day of winter break dad took me for Shark Bite ice cream, the blue one with the gummy sharks. It is still my favorite. Even in the winter. We sat by the window and watched people with big coats walk by. Dad asked what I wish for this new year. I said a puppy named Waffles, the diving board, and to finish my chapter book. Dad said those are good goals. He said his wish is that I keep being a good big brother. I said I can do that one easy.
entries.favorite: Making a new year wish on my ice cream
entries.highlight: Got Shark Bite ice cream with dad on winter break and made New Year wishes.

entries.title: A snowman with a shark fin
entries.body: It snowed a lot so after school me and Lucas built a snowman. I rolled the bottom ball and it got so big I could not push it anymore. Lucas made the head but it was kind of small. So our snowman has a tiny head. I made a shark fin out of snow and put it on top like a hat. Did you know some sharks live in really cold water, way under the ice? So a snow shark is kind of real. Lucas gave it his dinosaur's name. Now our snowman is called Roary the shark snowman. It does not make sense but it is funny.
entries.favorite: The shark fin on his head
entries.highlight: Built a snowman with a shark fin hat after school.

entries.title: Dogs who love the snow
entries.body: There were so many dogs at the snowy park today. One husky was so happy. He was digging tunnels in the snow with his nose. Then he rolled on his back and wiggled. His owner said huskies are made for snow. There was also a tiny dog in a coat who would not walk. Her owner had to carry her. I think Waffles would be in between. He would play in the snow for a little and then want to go inside for hot chocolate. Well, dog hot chocolate.
entries.highlight: Watched dogs dig and play in the snow at the park.

entries.title: Kai and the ice slide
entries.body: Me and Kai went to the park. The slide was frozen and super slippery. We went down so fast we flew off the end into the snow. Kai said this is the best slide in the world now. I said it was like the fast slide at the water park, but freezing. Then we made up a snow joke. Why did the snowman call his dog Frost? Because Frost bites! Kai made that one up himself for his joke book. He is writing a real joke book now with a cover. I am the first person who gets to read it.
entries.highlight: Played on a slippery frozen slide at the park with Kai.

entries.title: Ice skating with dad
entries.body: Dad took me ice skating for the first time. The skates were so tight and wobbly. When I stood on the ice my feet went in different directions. I fell three times right away. One time I fell on my bottom and it was so cold. Dad held both my hands and skated backwards. Then I held only one hand. At the end I went from the wall to dad all by myself. It was kind of like swimming to dad the first time. Scary but then you do it.
entries.favorite: Holding dad's hands on the ice
entries.highlight: Went ice skating with dad for the first time and kept trying after falling.

entries.title: A real talk with mom
entries.body: Tonight mom and me had a real talk. I told her sometimes I feel like Lucas gets all the attention. Because he is little and he needs help with everything. I did not want to say it because it sounded mean. But mom said thank you for telling me. She said feelings are not mean. Then she said let's have mom and me time every Thursday. Just us. Tonight we played cards and had tea with honey. I feel lighter, like when you take off a heavy backpack.
entries.favorite: Mom and me time on Thursdays
entries.highlight: Told mom he sometimes felt left out because Lucas needs so much help, and they started a weekly mom-and-me time.

entries.title: My new Laser job
entries.body: I got a new Laser job. Dad said since I am so good with food and water, I can try the litter box. It is kind of gross. You use a scoop and the clumps go in a bag. I held my nose the first time. Laser sat and watched me the whole time like a boss. I added a new box on my chart that says litter. Dad said puppies have a lot of poop jobs too. I said I know. I am ready for poop jobs.
entries.highlight: Took on the new job of scooping Laser's litter box as part of his pet responsibilities.

entries.title: Noah was sad and I noticed
entries.body: Noah came over to play but he was really quiet. He did not want to build anything. Usually he loves building. So I asked are you okay? He said his grandpa is in the hospital. I did not know what to say. Then I said my grandma says hospitals help people get better. And I said do you want to see Laser do her high five? He nodded. Laser did it and Noah smiled a little. Then we played quietly. Mom said I was a good friend today. I hope Noah's grandpa is okay.
entries.highlight: Noticed Noah was quiet during a playdate, asked what was wrong, and helped cheer him up.

entries.title: Practicing a snowy dog walk
entries.body: I asked mom for a puppy again. She said remember, puppies need walks even in snow. So I said okay. I put on my coat and boots and hat and walked around the whole block. In the snow! Mom watched from the window. My nose got so cold and runny. When I came back I said see, I can do it. Mom laughed and gave me a hug. She said you are very determined. I don't know what that means exactly, but I think it is good.
entries.favorite: Walking around the block in the snow
entries.highlight: Walked around the block in the snow to prove he could walk a puppy in bad weather.

entries.title: Making burger patties
entries.body: Tonight we had hamburgers and french fries. But dad cooked the burgers in a pan because it is too snowy for the grill. I helped make the patties. You take a ball of meat and squish it flat. Dad said make a little thumb dent in the middle so it does not puff up. I did not know that. My hands were so cold from the meat. Lucas wanted to help but he just poked holes in them. We baked the fries in the oven. They were crunchy.
entries.highlight: Helped dad shape hamburger patties for a winter burger night.

entries.title: Lucas played a real game
entries.body: At family game night Lucas played a real game for the first time. Not just on a team. It was the one with the ladders and slides. I explained the rules to him. You spin, you count the spaces, if you land on a ladder you go up. He counted out loud with his finger. Then he won! Fair and square. He did not even need help. He did a little dance. I was not mad at all. I remember when I always got grumpy when I lost. I was proud of him.
entries.highlight: Explained the rules of a board game to Lucas, who played his first real game and won.

entries.title: A snowman for Laser to see
entries.body: After school there was new snow so I built a snowman right outside the living room window. That way Laser can see it. I used two pine cones for eyes and a stick for a mouth. Then Laser came to the window and stared at it. Her tail got fluffy like she was scared. I think she thought it was a giant stranger. I knocked on the window and waved. She calmed down after a while. Then she fell asleep on the windowsill looking at it.
entries.highlight: Built a snowman right outside the window so Laser could watch it.

entries.title: Reading tent with Theo
entries.body: Theo came over after school. We built a tent in my room but this time it was a reading tent. We brought pillows and flashlights. Theo brought his book about sharks. I brought my first dog detective book. I am on chapter three. Some words are hard, like suspicious. Theo helped me sound it out. We read quietly for a long time. Then we did shark voices for the sharks in Theo's book. Mom peeked in and said I never thought I would see you two so quiet.
entries.highlight: Built a reading tent with Theo and they each read their books by flashlight.

entries.title: Movie night with a real ocean show
entries.body: For movie night we watched a show about the real ocean. Not a cartoon. It had a giant octopus that changed colors and squeezed through a tiny hole. Did you know an octopus can fit through any hole bigger than its beak, because it has no bones? I said it out loud and dad paused the show so I could explain. And there was a part about the deepest part of the ocean. It is so dark down there and there are anglerfish that glow. I used to be scared of deep water. I still think the deep ocean is scary but now it is kind of exciting too. Lucas fell asleep. Dad said that was the most educational movie night ever.
entries.highlight: Watched an ocean documentary for movie night and learned new sea animal facts.

entries.title: Mom and me hot chocolate date
entries.body: Me and mom time was on Wednesday this week because of dad's work. We went to the coffee shop and got hot chocolates. Mine had whipped cream and a little chocolate shaped like a heart because Valentine's Day is soon. I told mom all about my dog detective book. The dog is named Rex and he solves crimes with his nose. Mom asked who I think took the missing cake. I said the mailman, but I am not sure yet. Mom says she can't wait to find out. Then she asked what my next book should be. I said a shark detective. She said maybe you should write that one.
entries.highlight: Had a mom-and-me hot chocolate date at the coffee shop and talked about his chapter book.

entries.title: Heart French toast for mom
entries.body: Dad and me woke up early to make mom a Valentine's breakfast. Dad has a cookie cutter shaped like a heart, so we cut hearts out of the bread and dipped them in the eggs. I put red food coloring in some of the eggs so they would be pink. The first one stuck and came out like a broken heart. Dad said that one is for the chef. Then I flipped one all by myself with the big spatula and it landed perfect. Lucas put strawberries on top, but he ate every other one. We brought mom her plate on a tray. She said this is the sweetest Valentine ever. And she laughed and hugged us.
entries.favorite: Flipping the heart French toast myself
entries.highlight: Made heart-shaped French toast with dad as a Valentine's breakfast surprise for mom.

entries.title: Another puppy valentine
entries.body: Last year I made mom a puppy valentine. She said nice try buddy. This year I made a new one. It has a picture of me and Laser and a puppy. It says I have taken care of Laser for almost a whole year with no forgetting. Can we please think about a puppy? Mom read it two times. She did not say nice try. She said she will talk to dad. And she put it on the fridge next to my Laser chart. That is a good sign. I think.
entries.highlight: Gave mom another puppy valentine, a year after the first, and she kept it on the fridge.

entries.title: The puppy who pulled on the leash
entries.body: At the park today there was a puppy pulling so hard on his leash. His owner was a big man but the puppy was dragging him around. I laughed but then I thought, Waffles might do that. I asked the man how you stop the pulling. He said you stop walking every time he pulls, and he learns. I said thank you and I told mom on the way home. Mom said you are doing research now. I am. Puppy research.
entries.highlight: Watched an excited puppy pull its owner around the park and thought about leash training.

entries.title: Snow day snow tunnel
entries.body: SNOW DAY! The plow made a giant snow pile by the driveway. Dad helped me dig a tunnel through it. It took the whole morning. We used a shovel and a pot from the kitchen. When it was done I could crawl from one side to the other. It was blue and quiet inside, like being under the water in the deep end. Lucas crawled through too but he got scared halfway and backed out. So I went with him the second time, right behind him. He made it through. Then we had grilled cheese.
entries.highlight: Had a snow day and dug a tunnel through the big snow pile with dad.

entries.title: Laser finally uses the cat tree
entries.body: Laser finally used her cat tree! Remember she got it for Christmas and she only sat in the box? Mom finally recycled the box. So today Laser looked at the cat tree for a long time. Then she jumped to the first level. Then the second. Then the very top! She sat up there like a queen looking at everybody. Dad said maybe she was waiting for the box to leave. I put her feather toy on the top so she has something to do up there.
entries.highlight: Noticed Laser finally climbing her cat tree after months of preferring its box.

entries.title: Snow family with the neighbors
entries.body: It snowed again so we built a whole snow family in the front yard. A snow dad, a snow mom, a snow me and a snow Lucas. Then I made a little snow Laser with pointy ears. It was hard to make a tail so I used a stick. The neighbors came out and said it was so cute. One lady took a picture. Lucas said we need a snow Waffles. So we made a snow puppy too. Now the snow family has a puppy. At least the snow family does.
entries.highlight: Built a whole snow family in the front yard, including a small snow Laser.

entries.title: Lucas was nervous about preschool
entries.body: This morning Lucas did not want to go to preschool. He was crying and holding the door. He said he misses mom when he is there. I know how that feels, like the first day of second grade. So I gave him my shark tooth necklace. I said this is for good luck, and when you hold it you can be brave. He stopped crying and put it under his shirt. Mom said he wore it all day. When he came home he gave it back and said it worked.
entries.favorite: Giving Lucas my shark tooth necklace
entries.highlight: Helped Lucas feel brave about preschool by lending him his good-luck shark tooth necklace.

entries.title: I taught Lucas to make a snowman
entries.body: After school I taught Lucas how to make a snowman by himself. First you make a little snowball in your hands. Then you put it down and roll it, and it gets bigger and bigger. I showed him to pat it so it does not fall apart. Lucas did the bottom and the middle and the head all by himself. I only helped lift the head. He was so proud. He named it Matty. A snowman named after me! Mom said I am a really good teacher.
entries.favorite: Lucas rolling the head by himself
entries.highlight: Taught Lucas step by step how to build a snowman, and Lucas built one on his own.

entries.title: Teaching Lucas to feed Laser
entries.body: Lucas wanted to help with Laser jobs. He is almost four. So I showed him how to feed Laser. You use the little scoop. One scoop, not two. Laser will tell you she wants two but she only gets one. Lucas did it really careful and did not spill. I let him put the sticker on my chart. He picked a dinosaur sticker even though it is a star chart. That is okay. Laser rubbed on his legs. Lucas said she says thank you.
entries.highlight: Started teaching Lucas how to feed Laser and let him put a sticker on the chart.

entries.title: Last sledding of the winter
entries.body: Dad said this is probably the last good snow this winter. So we went sledding with Theo and Sofia at the big hill. We had races, like a hundred of them. Theo has a fast blue plastic sled he calls the Hammerhead and Sofia has the wooden kind. I won one race and Sofia won two. She lays down flat like a stingray to go faster. That is a smart idea. At the end we all went down together in a long sled train. We crashed at the bottom in a big pile and could not stop laughing.
entries.highlight: Went sledding with friends at the big hill, likely for the last time of the winter.

entries.title: Kai's joke book is finished
entries.body: Me and Kai went to the park, and it was a little muddy because all the snow is melting. Kai brought his joke book. It is finished! It has twenty-six jokes, one for every letter of the alphabet. He made the cover with markers and staples. And on the first page it says, for Matthew, who laughs the loudest. I did not know he was going to do that. I felt so happy I did not know what to say. So I just said thank you, and then I read the whole thing out loud on the bench. The Q joke is the best one. But the S joke is mine from first grade, the peanut butter and jellyfish one, and he wrote my name next to it. We laughed so loud a lady walking her dog laughed too.
entries.highlight: Went to the park with Kai, who finished his handmade joke book and dedicated it to him.

entries.title: Reading my chapter book at school
entries.body: At school we have independent reading time now. You can read any book you want. I am reading my first dog detective book, the one from Christmas. I am on chapter six of ten. It is getting really good. Rex the dog smelled frosting on the mailman's shoe, but it was a trick, because the mailman was at the bakery for a different reason. When Mr. Okafor said time is up I said can I please have five more minutes? He said that is the best question a teacher can hear. So he gave everyone five more minutes. Sofia said thanks Matthew.
entries.favorite: Reading time not being long enough
entries.highlight: Read his first real chapter book during independent reading time and asked for more time.

entries.title: Frozen yogurt with every topping
entries.body: After school dad took me and Lucas to the frozen yogurt place where you pick everything yourself. I got vanilla and strawberry swirled together. Then the toppings. I put gummy worms, of course, and mochi, and rainbow sprinkles. The gummy worms got frozen and hard and crunchy, which is a new way to eat them. Lucas got only sprinkles and yogurt, but like a mountain of sprinkles. They weigh it at the end. Mine was the heaviest. Dad said that is the most expensive froyo in history. I said it was worth it, and he said yeah it was.
entries.favorite: Gummy worms frozen on the yogurt
entries.highlight: Went to the frozen yogurt shop with dad and loaded his cup with toppings.

entries.title: Packing my own lunch
entries.body: Tonight I packed my own lunch for tomorrow. Mom watched but she did not help, except for the knife. I made a turkey and cheese sandwich and cut it into triangles because triangles taste better. That is a fact. I put in apple slices with a little lemon so they don't turn brown, which mom taught me. And then I made a snack bag with pretzels and three gummy worms. Only three, I promise. I wrote a note on the napkin that says have a good day Matthew. It is a note from me to me. Mom said that is very sweet and a little bit funny.
entries.highlight: Packed his own school lunch for the first time, including a sandwich and a homemade snack bag.

entries.title: Picking Lucas's birthday present
entries.body: Lucas is turning four on Sunday. Dad and me went to the store to pick his present. Last year I gave him my old shark book. This year I wanted to pick something new with my own money. I have nine dollars from my birthday card from grandma and the tooth fairy. We looked at trucks and balls and puzzles. Then I found a dinosaur book with flaps you can lift. Lucas loves dinosaurs now, even more than trucks. It was eight dollars. Dad said are you sure you want to spend almost all of it? I said yes. It is for Lucas. I wrapped it myself with too much tape.
entries.highlight: Went shopping with dad to pick out a birthday present for Lucas, who turns four.

entries.title: Noah's grandpa is home
entries.body: Noah came over and he was so happy. His grandpa came home from the hospital! He is still a little weak but he is home. Noah said thank you for being nice when I was sad. I said that is what friends do. Then we built the tallest Lego tower we ever made. It was taller than the table. We had to stand on a chair to put the top pieces on. Laser walked by and we both yelled no Laser! But she just sniffed it and left. It is still standing. I think it is a record. Noah wants to build one for his grandpa.
entries.highlight: Had a happy playdate with Noah after hearing his grandpa came home from the hospital.

entries.title: Laser and the shoe box
entries.body: I got new sneakers and they came in a shoe box. I put the box on the floor and you already know what happened. Laser got in. But she is bigger now than when she was a kitten. She did not really fit. Her back legs were in and her front legs were sticking out and her tail was hanging over the side. She looked so uncomfortable but she stayed there for an hour. Dad said if I fits, I sits, that is the cat rule. I took a picture and Lucas wants it on the fridge. Laser is almost one year old now. I can't believe she was so tiny.
entries.favorite: Laser squeezing in the tiny box
entries.highlight: Laughed watching Laser squeeze herself into a shoe box that was much too small.

entries.title: Laser's nine o'clock zoomies
entries.body: Every night around nine o'clock Laser gets the zoomies. Dad calls it the nine o'clock zoomies. She runs from the kitchen to the stairs and up the stairs and down the stairs, and her eyes get really big and black. Tonight she ran so fast on the kitchen floor she slid and crashed into the fridge. Then she sat down and licked her paw like it never happened. Lucas laughed so hard he got the hiccups, just like when he was little. I think the zoomies are because she sleeps all day. It is like she saved up all her running for night.
entries.highlight: Watched Laser get her usual nighttime zoomies and slide across the kitchen floor.

entries.title: Napping with Laser and my book
entries.body: On Saturday afternoon I was reading my dog detective book on the couch. Laser came up and lay down right on top of the book. Right on the words! I could not read anymore. So I put my head on the pillow and petted her. She started purring really loud. It makes your hand buzz. I think I fell asleep, because when I woke up the sun was in a different spot and mom had put a blanket on us. Laser was still there. I finished book one last night, so now I am on book two. Laser does not care about books. She cares about naps.
entries.highlight: Took an afternoon nap with Laser after reading together on the couch.

entries.title: Dad asked me questions about a puppy
entries.body: Today dad asked me questions about a puppy. Like a real interview. Who will walk it in the morning before school? I said me, I will wake up early. What happens when we go on vacation? I said grandma, like with Laser. What if the puppy chews your favorite thing? I said I will keep my stuff off the floor, which mom says I should do anyway. Dad wrote my answers on a paper. He said he is not saying yes. He is just thinking. But dad never thought about it before. Mom says maybe means almost yes, and thinking means almost maybe.
entries.highlight: Answered dad's serious questions about who would walk, feed, and train a puppy.

entries.title: Reading to Lucas at bedtime
entries.body: Tonight I read Lucas his bedtime story. Mom usually does it, but Lucas asked for me. He picked the dinosaur book I gave him for his birthday. I read every flap. I did voices for the dinosaurs, a deep voice for the big one and a squeaky voice for the little one. Lucas laughed and said again. I read it two times. Then he asked me to read my dog detective book. I read him one chapter. He fell asleep in the middle. I turned off his light and put his dinosaur next to him. I remember when he used to knock down all my towers. Now he wants me to read to him.
entries.highlight: Read Lucas a bedtime story from the dinosaur book he got for his birthday.

entries.title: First popsicle of spring, again
entries.body: Today was the first warm day of spring, so mom said popsicles on the porch, just like last year. I remember last year Lucas dropped his in the grass and cried, and I gave him one bite of mine because of the sharing rule. This year he held his with two hands the whole time and did not drop it. He is four now, so he is a lot better at popsicles. I got cherry, the shark fin kind, and he got blue raspberry. His whole tongue turned blue and he kept sticking it out at the mailman. The mailman stuck his tongue out back. That was the funniest part of the day. Mine still melted down my arm though. Some things never change. Laser watched us from the window the whole time with her tail going swish, swish, like she wanted a lick too.
entries.highlight: Had the first popsicles of spring with Lucas on the porch, a year after the first warm-day popsicle.

entries.title: Laser packed herself in my suitcase
entries.body: We are going to grandma's for spring break, so I was packing my suitcase. I put in my shirts and my pajamas and my swim trunks, because grandma's town has an indoor pool. Then I went to get my toothbrush. When I came back Laser was in the suitcase, lying right on my pajamas. She looked at me like, I am coming too. I said Laser, you can't come, grandma's neighbor is going to feed you. She did not move. I had to lift her out and she was all floppy like a noodle. Then she got back in. We did that three times. Finally I closed the lid and she sat on top of it instead. Cats really do not want you to leave.
entries.highlight: Found Laser curled up in his suitcase while packing for a spring break trip to grandma's.

entries.title: Drawing Laser with shapes
entries.body: In art class our teacher showed us a trick. You draw animals with shapes first. Circles for the head, an oval for the body, and long rectangles for the legs. Then you draw over the shapes and erase them. So after school I tried it on Laser while she was sitting by the window. Her legs finally look like legs and not like a table! The ears were good too, because I practiced them before. The tail I made curly like always. It is still not perfect. Cats are still hard to draw, especially the face. But mom said, this one looks like her, and I could tell she meant it this time, not just a mom saying it. I hung it in my room.
entries.highlight: Used a shape trick from art class to draw Laser, and her legs finally looked right.

entries.title: First grill night of the year
entries.body: Tonight dad got the grill out for the first time since fall. It was a little chilly, but dad said burger season is open. This time I got to use the big spatula and flip my own burger. Dad stood right next to me because the grill is very hot. You have to slide the spatula all the way under, or it breaks. Mine stayed in one piece. I made the thumb dent in the middle like dad taught me in the winter. We had french fries from the oven and corn. I put cheese and pickles on my burger. Lucas only eats the bun and the cheese. He says the burger part is too brown. I told him I used to be picky too.
entries.highlight: Helped dad grill the first burgers of the spring and flipped his own patty with the spatula.

entries.title: Helping Lucas on his balance bike
entries.body: After dinner I helped Lucas with his balance bike. It is the kind with no pedals, where you push with your feet. He kept putting his feet down every two seconds. I said try to lift your feet and glide, like when you go down a slide. I ran next to him on the sidewalk, like dad ran next to me when the training wheels came off. And then he lifted his feet and went like ten whole feet! He yelled Matty, did you see? I said yes, that was amazing! Dad came out and clapped. Lucas wants to do it every day now. I think he will be riding a real bike before he is five.
entries.highlight: Helped Lucas practice on his balance bike, coaching him the way dad coached him.

entries.title: Laser and the spider on the ceiling
entries.body: There was a spider on the ceiling above my bed, and Laser saw it. She sat on my bed and stared at it and made a weird noise. It sounds like ack ack ack, really fast, with her teeth. Dad said that is called chattering, and cats do it when they see something they want to hunt but can't reach. I did not know that. Ruby probably knows that. The spider was small and I did not really want it near my bed. But I also did not want Laser to eat it. So dad caught it in a cup and I took it outside to the bushes. Laser looked at the ceiling for the rest of the night just in case it came back.
entries.highlight: Watched Laser make chattering noises at a spider she could not reach.

entries.title: My first book report
entries.body: Today I gave my first book report. It was about the first dog detective book, the first chapter book I ever read all by myself. I made a poster with Rex the dog and a magnifying glass and the cake that went missing. I told the class the main characters, the problem, and how Rex solved it. I did not tell the ending, because Mr. Okafor said don't spoil it. Three kids asked if they can borrow it. Mr. Okafor said I spoke clearly and looked at the audience. My hands were a little shaky at first, but then it was fun. Last year I read a picture book to the class and got stuck on octopus. This year I talked about a whole chapter book.
entries.favorite: Everyone wanting to borrow my book
entries.highlight: Gave his first book report to the class on the first chapter book he read all by himself.

entries.title: Saturday breakfast for the whole family
entries.body: This morning dad and me made breakfast for everybody. I cracked all the eggs into the bowl, six eggs, and no shell got in. Not even one tiny piece. When I was six I always got shell in. Then I whisked them with a fork really fast. Dad let me stir them in the pan with the rubber spatula. You have to go slow so they get fluffy. I made toast and put butter on it while it was hot so it melts. Lucas set the forks, but he put them on the wrong side. Then I brought mom her plate in bed. She said, is this a hotel? I said yes, it is the Matthew hotel.
entries.highlight: Made scrambled eggs and toast for the family on Saturday morning with dad's help.

entries.title: Planning Laser's gotcha day
entries.body: In nine days it will be one year since Laser came home. Mom calls it her gotcha day. I want to have a little party for her. I made a list: one, a new toy mouse, because she lost the old one under the fridge. Two, a little bit of tuna. Three, a card. I made the card today with a picture of a tuna can, because Laser loves tuna more than anything. I wrote happy gotcha day Laser, love Matthew. Lucas signed it too, but it just looks like an L and a squiggle. Mom said cats don't understand birthdays. I said, she will understand tuna. Mom laughed and said that is true.
entries.highlight: Started planning a celebration for the one-year anniversary of Laser coming home.

entries.title: Crabbing at the edge of the dock
entries.body: Dad and me went crabbing at the bay again. Last year I sat in the middle of the dock because the water looked so dark and scary. This year I sat right at the edge with my feet hanging over. It is funny how something can be scary and then just be normal. I tied the chicken on the string myself this time. It was slimy and it was gross, but I did it. And then my string pulled! I pulled it up really slow, and it was a little crab, blue and green with tiny claws. Dad said it is a blue crab. Did you know blue crabs turn red when you cook them? We didn't cook this one. My first crab ever! Dad took a picture and then we let it go back in the water, because it was a baby. I said bye little guy, grow up big.
entries.highlight: Went crabbing with dad, sat at the edge of the dock this time, and caught his first crab.

entries.title: Ruby's fizzy geyser experiment
entries.body: Ruby came over and we made a fizzy geyser for fun. Ruby brought the instructions. We built it out of clay around a bottle and painted it gray like a rock. Then you put baking soda inside, and some red food coloring, and pour in vinegar. Ruby explained it is a reaction, because the vinegar is an acid. It foamed up and over the top and down the sides like a giant wave of sea foam. It went on the table and on the floor. Laser came to look and got some foam on her paw and shook it like crazy. We did it three more times until the vinegar was gone. Ruby is going to be a scientist or an animal doctor. Maybe both.
entries.highlight: Made a baking soda geyser with Ruby during a playdate after school.

entries.title: Kickball team captain
entries.body: At recess we played kickball, and I was a team captain for the first time. Usually the captains pick the fast kids first, and then some kids get picked last, and they look sad. I remember the time I got picked last at the park. It felt bad. So I had an idea. I picked Theo first, but then I picked a kid named Caleb who always gets picked last. Caleb kicked the ball really far, like a hundred feet, and got to second base. Everybody cheered. Mr. Okafor saw me at the end of recess and said, that was a kind way to be a captain. Our team lost by one point, but I did not even care that much.
entries.favorite: Picking everyone so nobody was last
entries.highlight: Was a team captain in recess kickball and made sure no one got picked last.

entries.title: Making a comic with Kai
entries.body: Kai came over and we made a comic book together. It is about a shark detective named Finn, because I love sharks and detectives, and Kai loves jokes. I did the drawings and Kai did the speech bubbles. In the story someone stole all the seaweed from the reef, and Finn has to find out who. It was a sneaky crab. Kai made the crab say things like, I'm feeling a little shellfish. I laughed every time. We did eight pages. It is the longest thing we ever made. Mom read it and said she wants a copy. We are going to make part two next time.
entries.highlight: Made a comic book with Kai about a shark detective, combining both of their favorite things.

entries.title: Laser's gotcha day nap
entries.body: We had Laser's gotcha day party a few days late, because of school. I gave her the new toy mouse and a little bit of tuna on a plate. She ate the tuna in two seconds and licked the plate until it squeaked. She played with the mouse for exactly one minute. Then she curled up on my bed and took a nap for the whole afternoon. Mom said that is the perfect cat party. I read her card to her and she did not wake up. I lay next to her for a while. A year ago she was so tiny she could sleep on my foot. Now she takes up half my pillow. And a year ago I kept forgetting her breakfast, and now I never do.
entries.favorite: Laser eating tuna and then napping
entries.highlight: Celebrated Laser's one-year gotcha day with tuna and a new toy mouse, and then she took a long nap.

entries.title: Rainy day science center
entries.body: It rained all day, so no outside recess again. But Mr. Okafor has a science center in our room, with a magnifying glass and a bug box. Before school Sofia found three worms on the sidewalk, because worms come up when it rains. Mr. Okafor let us put them in the bug box with wet dirt. I looked at one with the magnifying glass. It has little rings all over its body, like a hundred of them. Ruby told me once that worms breathe through their skin, so I told Sofia. Then I told her one of my own. Did you know there are worms in the ocean too? Some live way down deep by hot cracks in the sea floor where the sun never goes, and they are bright red and as tall as me. I saw a picture of them at the aquarium. Sofia said, how do you know all this stuff? I said, half from Ruby and half from my ocean books. At the end of the day we put the worms back in the garden so they could go home. I named them first, because Lucas would want me to. Squiggle, Noodle, and Captain. It was a good rainy day.
entries.favorite: Watching the worms after the rain
entries.highlight: Had indoor recess on a rainy day and looked at worms from the playground in the science center.

entries.title: The first water fight of the year
entries.body: It got really warm after school, almost like summer, so Kai came over and we had the first water fight of the year. The water was still freezing cold from the hose. Kai screamed so loud the neighbor looked over the fence. We had squirt guns and a bucket. Lucas wanted to play, so I gave him my second squirt gun, the good one, because his little one doesn't go very far. He got Kai right in the ear. Kai yelled pickles like he always does. When we were done we all lay on the deck in the sun to dry off. We were shivering and laughing at the same time.
entries.highlight: Had the first backyard water fight of the year with Kai on a surprisingly warm May afternoon.

entries.title: Washing cars for my puppy fund
entries.body: I have a jar on my shelf now that says Puppy Fund. Dad said if we ever get a puppy, I can use the money to buy his first collar and toys. So today after school dad and me washed his car and mom's car in the driveway, and the neighbor paid me two dollars to wash hers too! I did the doors and the windows and the tires. The tires are the dirtiest part. I used the old toothbrush on the little holes. Now my jar has fourteen dollars and fifty cents. I counted it three times to make sure. Dad said a puppy collar is about twelve dollars. So I can already buy one. I just need the puppy.
entries.favorite: Counting the money in my jar
entries.highlight: Washed cars in the driveway with dad to earn money for his puppy fund jar.

entries.title: Lucas made me a birthday card
entries.body: Tomorrow is my birthday, but Lucas could not wait. He gave me his card tonight. He made it himself at preschool. On the front there is a picture of me swimming in a big blue square, and the square is the deep end. He told me that's you, because you are brave. Inside it says happy birthday Matty in his wobbly letters. His teacher helped him with the y. I almost cried, but a happy cry. I told him it is the best card I ever got, and it is true. I put it on my shelf next to my puppy fund jar and Practice Waffles. It is funny, when he was two I used to say he was annoying. Now he is one of my favorite people.
entries.highlight: Received an early birthday card from Lucas showing him swimming in the deep end.

entries.title: My eighth birthday pool party
entries.body: It was my birthday! I am eight now. I had a pool party at the indoor pool again, just like last year. But this year was so different. Last year I wore floaties and stayed in the shallow part while Sofia jumped in the deep end. This year I jumped in the deep end with everybody! Theo and Kai and Sofia and Noah and Ruby and me all held hands and jumped at the same time. Then we played sharks and minnows. The cake was shaped like a hammerhead shark, with gray frosting and gummy sharks all around it. When everybody sang, Lucas sang the loudest again. He always does. Grandma gave me goggles that are blue and the strap doesn't pull my hair. Eight feels big.
entries.favorite: Jumping in the deep end with everybody
entries.highlight: Turned eight and celebrated with an indoor pool party where he jumped into the deep end with his friends.

entries.title: A new frisbee trick
entries.body: Dad and me went to the park after school with the frisbee. I can throw it really far now, like across the whole soccer field, almost. Dad taught me a new trick. When it comes to you, you lift one leg and catch it under your leg. The first time it hit me in the knee. The second time it fell on the grass. The third time I caught it! Dad yelled, that's a highlight reel catch! A guy walking his dog clapped. Last year I was just learning to flick my wrist. Now I am doing tricks. I want to show Theo at recess, but I have to practice more first so I don't look silly.
entries.highlight: Learned to catch a frisbee under his leg while playing with dad at the park.

entries.title: Laser's fly hunt
entries.body: A fly got in the kitchen today and Laser went crazy. She jumped on the counter, which she is not allowed to do. Then she jumped on the chair, then the table. The fly kept buzzing around the light. Mom was trying to swat it with a dish towel, and Laser was trying to catch it, and the two of them kept almost bumping into each other. It looked like a cartoon. Then Laser jumped really high and clapped her paws together and caught it! In the air! Mom said, well, Laser wins. I was kind of grossed out, but also impressed. Lucas said Laser is a superhero. I said a super hunter.
entries.favorite: Laser catching the fly in midair
entries.highlight: Watched Laser chase a fly around the kitchen until she finally caught it in midair.

entries.title: I stood up for Lucas at the park
entries.body: Me and Noah were at the park, and mom brought Lucas too. Lucas was waiting for the slide, and a bigger kid pushed him out of the way. Lucas fell down and started crying. I felt so mad, like my face was on fire. But I remembered what mom says, be strong but be kind. So I walked over and I said, hey, that is my brother, and he was waiting. You can't push people. The kid looked surprised and he said sorry, and went to the swings. Then I helped Lucas up and checked his hands. Only a little scrape. Noah said that was really brave. Lucas held my hand all the way home. Mom said she was proud of how I used my words.
entries.favorite: Lucas holding my hand on the way home
entries.highlight: Stood up calmly to an older kid who pushed Lucas at the park, then made sure Lucas was okay.

entries.title: Grandma's cookout and the corn contest
entries.body: We went to grandma's for a cookout. It is Memorial Day weekend, so the pool opens tomorrow! Grandma made corn on the cob, ribs, potato salad, and her watermelon triangles. Dad and me had a corn eating race. You have to go row by row like a typewriter. Grandma says that, and I don't know what a typewriter is, but okay. I won by one row! I had corn in my teeth for the whole night. Lucas swallowed a watermelon seed again, and this time he was not worried. He said, Grandma said no watermelon grows in your tummy. He remembered from last year. Grandma's pie rule is now three green beans, because I am eight.
entries.highlight: Ate dinner at grandma's Memorial Day weekend cookout and won a corn-on-the-cob race against dad.

entries.title: Field day snack table
entries.body: Today was field day at school! We did a sack race and a water balloon toss and tug of war. My class won tug of war against the other second grade class, because we all leaned back at the same time. My favorite part was the snack table though. They had orange slices that were ice cold and so juicy. I ate like eight of them. Then you put the peel in your mouth and smile and it looks like orange teeth. Theo and me took a picture like that. There were also freezer pops in every color. I got blue, because blue is ocean color. Field day means the school year is almost over. I am excited, but I will miss Mr. Okafor.
entries.highlight: Ran races at the end-of-year field day and loved the orange slices at the snack table.

entries.title: Teaching Lucas to float
entries.body: After school we went to the pool, because it is open now. Lucas still wears floaties, just like I used to. He is scared of putting his head back in the water. So I said, I will teach you to float. I held his back like Miss Marina held my back last summer. I said, put your tummy up to the sky. Those are the exact words she said to me. He was stiff like a board at first and he kept lifting his head. Then he relaxed, and I took my hands away just a little, and he was floating, with his floaties but still. He said Matty, I'm floating! I said, you are! Mom took a video. I feel like a real swim teacher.
entries.highlight: Taught Lucas to float on his back at the pool, using the same words his swim teacher once used.

entries.title: Last day of second grade
entries.body: Last day of school! Second grade is done. We signed each other's shirts again, like last year. This time I can write in cursive, sort of. Theo wrote, see you at the pool, shark boy, same as always. Sofia drew a perfect Laser. Mr. Okafor gave everybody a note. Mine said, Matthew, you went from picture books to chapter books this year, and you were a kind friend. Keep reading and keep being kind. I read it in the car three times. Mr. Okafor's shark bow tie was on, because it was a special day. I hugged him at the door. Now it is pool time all summer again. Third grade next. That sounds so old.
entries.highlight: Finished second grade, signed shirts with friends, and received a note from Mr. Okafor about his reading.

entries.title: Showing Theo the leg catch
entries.body: After the last day, Theo came over and we played frisbee in the backyard to celebrate. I finally showed him the leg catch. I practiced it a lot, so I only missed once. Theo said, okay, teach me. So I taught him like dad taught me. Lift your leg, keep your eye on it, and don't be scared of it. He got hit in the knee like I did. Then on his sixth try he got it! We did a big celebration dance. We played until mom called us for pizza. We made a summer list. Swim every day, build a hideout in the woods, catch the biggest crab, and jump off the diving board. Theo already can. I have not yet.
entries.highlight: Celebrated the end of school by playing frisbee with Theo and showing him the trick catch.

entries.title: Fruit popsicles with Lucas
entries.body: Me and Lucas made our own popsicles again, but this time with real fruit. Last year we just used juice and Lucas's looked brown. This year mom bought strawberries and blueberries and kiwi. I cut the strawberries with the kid knife and Lucas put the blueberries in the molds. He counted them out loud, one, two, three, four, and then ate the fifth one. Then we poured in lemonade. I showed him not to fill it all the way, because when water freezes it gets bigger. Ruby told me that. Lucas did not believe me, so he filled one all the way to the top. When it froze it was a little bit puffed out the top. He said, oh, you were right. Then I told him, did you know that is why icebergs float? Ice is lighter than water, so the ocean freezes on the top and the sea animals keep swimming underneath. Ruby told me the first part, and the iceberg part I read in my ocean book.
entries.highlight: Made homemade popsicles with real fruit and taught Lucas how to fill the molds.

entries.title: Backyard camping with Lucas
entries.body: Last night dad set up the tent in the backyard and me and Lucas slept in it with him! It is Lucas's first time camping. We had flashlights and sleeping bags and s'mores from the fire pit. My marshmallow caught on fire, but I blew it out and it was still good, just extra crunchy. Lucas got scared when an owl hooted. I told him owls are nice, and they can turn their heads almost all the way around. That is a Ruby fact from a long time ago. Then he asked me about the stars, and I showed him the Big Dipper, because dad showed me. I said, did you know sailors used the stars to find their way across the ocean? Lucas said, like a map in the sky. He fell asleep holding my sleeve. Dad snored so loud. I think the owl was scared of dad.
entries.favorite: Lucas asking me about the stars
entries.highlight: Camped in a tent in the backyard with Lucas and dad, and told Lucas about the stars.

entries.title: Watching Lucas's first swim lesson
entries.body: Today Lucas had his first swim lesson. And guess what, his teacher is Miss Marina! The same one I had. She remembered me. She said, are you the brave one who floated first? I said yes, and now I swim in the deep end. I sat on the bleachers with mom and watched Lucas. He was on the steps, just like I was. He looked so nervous, and I knew exactly how he felt, because my tummy felt funny on my first day too. Then he put his face in and blew bubbles. I gave him a thumbs up and he gave me one back. After, I told him, you did great, the first lesson is the hardest. He said, was it hard for you? I said, so hard.
entries.highlight: Watched Lucas's first swim lesson from the bleachers and remembered his own first lesson.

entries.title: Ruby and the nature journal
entries.body: I went to Ruby's house, and she showed me her nature journal. You write down animals and plants you find and draw them. So she gave me a notebook and we started one for me too. We went to her garden and looked under the leaves. We found a toad! It was brown and bumpy and its throat was going in and out. Ruby said toads are not the same as frogs, toads have drier skin. I drew it with the shape trick from art class. Circles and ovals. It was actually good! Then we found two ladybugs and a snail. I wrote everything down with the date. Ruby said a real scientist always writes the date. I want to fill the whole notebook this summer. I saved the last pages just for ocean animals, for when we go to the beach.
