entries.highlight: Started a nature journal with Ruby and found a toad in her garden.

entries.title: Father's Day water fight
entries.body: Today was Father's Day. Dad said the only thing he wanted was a water fight. So me and Lucas and mom made a plan in secret. I made us water balloon bombs. Lucas was the distraction. He went up to dad and said, daddy, look at this rock. And while dad was looking, mom came from behind and dumped the whole bucket on his head! Dad yelled so loud! Then he grabbed the hose and chased all of us. I got soaked, but it was worth it. We gave dad the card I made. It has a picture of us crabbing and my first blue crab. Dad said it was the best Father's Day ever. Then he said, but I am getting you back.
entries.favorite: Dad getting the bucket on his head
entries.highlight: Celebrated Father's Day with a backyard water fight where dad got a surprise bucket of water.

entries.title: Trail mix for the hike
entries.body: We went on a hike in the woods today, and I made the trail mix. I put peanuts, raisins, pretzels, cheerios, and chocolate chips. I tried to make it fair so there would be chocolate chips for everybody. When I was little I would pick out all the chocolate first. I still wanted to, but I did not. Well, only two times. The hike was long, and there was a stream with stepping stones. Lucas got tired so dad carried him on his shoulders. At the top there was a big rock where you could see far, and we ate the trail mix there. Mom said it is the best trail mix she ever had. I think she was just really hungry.
entries.highlight: Made his own trail mix for a family hike and tried not to eat all the chocolate.

entries.title: Laser and the bird at the window
entries.body: A bird landed on the bird feeder by the window, and Laser saw it. She went super low, like she was flat on the floor, and she crawled to the window really slowly. Then she wiggled her bottom, which means she is about to jump. I knew it would happen, because I have watched her do it like a hundred times with her mouse. She jumped and hit the window with her paws, bump, and the bird flew away. Laser sat there acting like she meant to do that. I wrote it in my nature journal: a cardinal, red, and Laser tried to catch it. Then I drew Laser at the window. I wrote, cats can't help it, they are hunters. Ruby said that is a good scientist note.
entries.highlight: Watched Laser hunt a bird through the window and noticed how she wiggles before she pounces.

entries.title: Nature journal at the park
entries.body: Me and Ruby took our nature journals to the park by the pond. We sat quiet on the bench for a long time, which is hard for me, but Ruby says animals come out when you are quiet. And then a big gray bird landed in the water. It had long legs and a long neck and it stood so still. Ruby whispered that it is a heron, and it is hunting. Then it stuck its beak in the water so fast and came out with a minnow! I could not believe it. It reminded me of the pelicans at the aquarium. Did you know a pelican's pouch can hold more water than its stomach can? I drew it and wrote the date. I have eleven pages now. The heron is my favorite page. Ruby said we should come back every week and see what changes. I said yes, a summer experiment.
entries.favorite: Seeing a heron at the pond
entries.highlight: Filled pages of his nature journal with Ruby at the park pond, including a heron.

entries.title: A hideout in the woods with Theo
entries.body: Me and Theo built a hideout in the woods behind the park, from our summer list. We found a big tree that fell down, and we leaned sticks against it to make walls, like a teepee. It took us all morning. Theo found the long sticks and I wove leaves between them so it would be shady. Inside there was room for both of us to sit. We brought granola bars and water. Theo said it is our headquarters. Then we heard a crunching noise and we froze. It was just a squirrel. We laughed at ourselves for being scared. Theo's dad came to check on us and said it was very well built. We crossed it off the list. Next is the diving board.
entries.highlight: Built a stick hideout in the woods behind the park with Theo, checking off their summer list.

entries.title: Frisbee at the lake beach
entries.body: We went to the beach at the lake today. It is not the ocean, but it has sand. Me and dad played frisbee on the sand, and when you dive for it, the sand is soft so it doesn't hurt. I dove like ten times, even when I didn't need to. Then dad threw one too high and it went in the water. I ran in and swam to get it. Dad said, look at you, last year you wouldn't even go near the dark water on the dock. I didn't even think about it. I just went. Lucas buried mom's feet in the sand and put shells on top. I found a little snail shell for my nature journal. I told Lucas, did you know hermit crabs move into bigger shells when they grow? He said, like when we get a bigger house. My shoulders got a little pink even with sunscreen.
entries.favorite: Diving for the frisbee in the sand
entries.highlight: Played frisbee on the sandy lake beach with the family and waded in to get it.

entries.title: Mom and me talk about the diving board
entries.body: Tonight was mom and me time, even though it is Wednesday. We sat on the porch with lemonade. I told her that I want to jump off the diving board, but every time I get in line my tummy flips. Theo can do it, Sofia can do it, even Noah did it last week. Mom said when she was a kid, she climbed up the ladder three times and climbed back down before she jumped. I said really? She said yes, and the fourth time she jumped, and then she did it fifty more times that summer. She said being scared just means it matters to you. I think I am going to try on the Fourth of July. Mom said she will be there watching. She did not say I have to.
entries.favorite: Mom telling me about her first jump
entries.highlight: Talked with mom about being nervous for the diving board, and she shared her own story.

entries.title: I jumped off the diving board
entries.body: I JUMPED OFF THE DIVING BOARD! It was the Fourth of July and the pool was so crowded. I got in line. I climbed the ladder, and when I got to the top the water looked so far down. I almost climbed back down like mom did when she was little. The lifeguard said, take your time, buddy. I looked over and saw mom and dad and Lucas waving. And then I just walked to the end and jumped. I went down down down, and the water went up my nose, and then I came up and everybody was cheering, even people I don't know. Lucas yelled MATTY loud enough for the whole pool. Then I got right back in line and did it again. The second one was not even scary. Two summers ago I wore floaties in the shallow end.
entries.highlight: Jumped off the diving board for the first time on the Fourth of July after climbing up and almost turning back.

entries.title: Keeping Laser calm during fireworks
entries.body: Tonight there were fireworks, and Laser does not like the booms. Last year she hid under the bed and would not come out until the next day. So this year I made a plan. I made her a cave out of a blanket and a chair in my room, with her favorite towel inside. Then I sat next to it and read my book out loud to her in a calm voice, so she could hear me instead of the booms. Mom and dad watched the fireworks from the porch with Lucas. I could see some from my window. Laser stayed in her cave the whole time, but she was purring, not shaking. Mom came in after and said, that was a really thoughtful thing to do. I said it was my job. I am her person.
entries.highlight: Stayed home with Laser during the loud fireworks and made her a cozy hiding spot.

entries.title: Movie night after the big jump
entries.body: Tonight was movie night, but before the movie, dad put the video of my diving board jump on the TV. It was so big on the screen! You can see me at the top of the ladder looking down for a long time. Then I walk to the end and jump, and you can hear Lucas yell MATTY. We watched it like four times. I noticed my legs were shaking at the top. I didn't know that until I saw it. Mom said that is what brave looks like, scared but doing it anyway. Then we watched a movie about a boy who trains a dragon. Lucas sat on my lap even though he is getting too big. Laser sat on mom. Everybody had a spot.
entries.highlight: Had a family movie night and watched the video of his diving board jump before the movie.

entries.title: A Pomeranian at the park
entries.body: There were so many dogs at the park today, but the best one was a Pomeranian. I never knew that kind before. It was small and orange and so fluffy, like a dandelion with legs. Its tail curled up over its back. The owner said Pomeranians are small but they think they are big, and they are very loyal. It sniffed my shoes and then it let me pet it. Its fur was so soft my hand disappeared in it. I asked the owner if they are good with cats. She said hers lives with two cats and they are best friends. I told mom on the way home that I think Waffles might be a Pomeranian. Mom said, that's a lot of fur to brush. I said I like brushing.
entries.highlight: Met a fluffy little Pomeranian at the park and decided that might be the perfect kind of dog.

entries.title: Strawberry ice cream at the farm stand
entries.body: We drove out to the farm stand where they make their own ice cream. They had strawberry with real strawberry pieces from their own field. I usually get Shark Bite, the blue one with the gummy sharks, because Shark Bite is my forever favorite. But I thought, I should try something new, like the cookie dough when I was six. So I got strawberry. It was pink and creamy, and the strawberry pieces were a little frozen and chewy. It might be tied with Shark Bite now. I can't decide. Lucas got chocolate and wore most of it on his chin. We sat on a hay bale and watched the cows. One cow mooed really loud right when Lucas took a bite and he jumped and his scoop almost fell. I caught his cone. Good reflexes from frisbee.
entries.favorite: Ice cream with real strawberry pieces
entries.highlight: Got homemade strawberry ice cream at a farm stand and decided it rivaled Shark Bite.

entries.title: Catching a bigger crab with dad
entries.body: Dad and me went crabbing again, early in the morning when the bay was all foggy. It was so quiet. Dad said crabs like the morning. I tied on my own chicken without even saying ew. And then I caught a crab that was way bigger than my first one, it was huge! It came out of the water snapping its claws and dad said pull slow, pull slow! I pulled and pulled and my arms were burning. When we got it in the bucket, dad was even more excited than me. We measured it on the ruler, seven inches across. We took a picture and let it go. I wrote it in my nature journal with the date, like Ruby does. On the way home we stopped for donuts. It was a perfect morning.
entries.highlight: Went back to the bay with dad and caught a much bigger crab than his first one.

entries.title: Lucas has his own Laser job now
entries.body: Lucas has been helping me feed Laser since the winter, but today he got his own job for real. He is in charge of the water bowl. I helped him make his own chart, like the one I made when I was seven. His has dinosaur stickers, of course. I showed him how to dump the old water, rinse the bowl, and fill it to the line, not too much or it spills. He did it so serious, with his tongue sticking out. Then he put the sticker on and said, I'm responsible now. I said, you are, but you have to do it every single day, even when you are excited about something. I know about that. My brain used to forget when I was excited. Laser drank right away like she was testing him.
entries.highlight: Gave Lucas his own small Laser job and helped him make his own sticker chart.

entries.title: I made the burgers by myself
entries.body: Tonight I made the hamburgers. Not helping, making. Dad said he would just be the safety guy. I made the patties myself, with the thumb dent, and put salt and pepper on them. Then I put them on the grill with the big spatula and set a timer for four minutes on each side. I flipped them all and only one broke a little. Dad put the cheese on at the end because of the heat. I also made the fries, the frozen kind in the oven, and I shook the pan halfway so they get crispy on both sides. Everybody said they were delicious. Lucas even ate a little bit of the burger part this time. I think he ate it because I made it. Dad said he is out of a job.
entries.favorite: Dad being the helper this time
entries.highlight: Made the burger patties and grilled them with dad only watching, a big step from helping last year.

entries.title: Water park vacation, part two
entries.body: We went back to the water park for vacation! Last year I wore a life jacket in the wave pool and I skipped the steep slide. This year I swam in the wave pool without a life jacket, and I took Lucas in the shallow part where the waves are small. He held my hands and jumped every wave and screamed every time. I rode the twisty tube slide like six times, and a new one where you go in a big bowl and spin around. I really wanted to try the super steep straight down one. I walked all the way up the stairs. But there was a height line, and I was one inch too short! One inch! I was a little disappointed, but also a little relieved, to be honest. Dad said next time for sure. I am going to eat a lot of vegetables.
entries.favorite: The wave pool without a life jacket
entries.highlight: Returned to the water park for vacation, rode much more than last year, and helped Lucas in the wave pool.

entries.title: Writing instructions for grandma
entries.body: Grandma is taking care of Laser while we are at the water park. Last summer when we came home I forgot Laser's water and she drank from the faucet. I still remember that. So this time, before we left, I wrote grandma instructions. One scoop of food in the morning and one at night. Fresh water every day, filled to the line. Scoop the litter. Laser likes the feather toy at nine o'clock when she gets the zoomies. She hides when there is thunder, so check under my bed. I taped it to the fridge right next to the charts. Tonight grandma texted mom a picture of Laser eating, and she wrote, your son's instructions are better than a babysitter's. I felt proud. I miss Laser though.
entries.highlight: Wrote detailed Laser care instructions for grandma before vacation, and grandma said they were perfect.

entries.title: Sharing a hotel bed with Lucas
entries.body: At the hotel me and Lucas had to share a bed. When I was little I would have said no way, because he kicks. He still kicks. But it was kind of fun. After mom and dad turned off the lights, we whispered jokes under the blanket. I told him Kai's jokes from his joke book. He doesn't get most of them, but he laughs anyway because I laugh. Then he made up his own joke. Why did the dinosaur cross the road? Because he was a dinosaur. It makes no sense, but I laughed so hard that dad said, boys, sleep. In the morning Lucas was sideways with his feet on my face. Mom took a picture. I am going to show him that when he is a teenager.
entries.highlight: Shared a hotel bed with Lucas on vacation and stayed up whispering jokes.

entries.title: Back to the pond with Ruby
entries.body: Me and Ruby went back to the pond for our summer experiment. It has been almost a month since we saw the heron. We sat on the same bench and wrote down what changed. The cattails are taller now and the water is lower because it hasn't rained. And there were baby ducks! Seven of them following their mom in a line. Ruby said they are called ducklings and they can swim right after they hatch. Right after! I needed lessons and Miss Marina. We did not see the heron this time, but we saw a turtle sitting on a log in the sun. I drew it. My journal has twenty pages now. Ruby has thirty-one, but she started before me. Ruby said comparing is not the point. She is right.
entries.highlight: Returned to the park pond with Ruby for their summer journal experiment and saw how things had changed.

entries.title: Helping Lucas in the shallow end
entries.body: At the pool today I spent a long time in the shallow end with Lucas. Mom asked if I wanted to go to the diving board with Theo, and I did, but Lucas asked me to help him. So I stayed with him first. He took his floaties off, and I stood four steps away, like dad did for me two summers ago. I said, swim to me, face in, kick kick kick. He did it! He was splashing a lot and his kicks were kind of wild, but he touched my hands. Then I backed up one more step. He did it again. He came up coughing a little but smiling. I told him that's exactly how I learned. After that I went to the diving board and did a cannonball. Lucas cheered from the shallow end.
entries.highlight: Helped Lucas practice swimming in the shallow end without floaties, the way dad once helped him.

entries.title: Frisbee golf at the park
entries.body: Dad found out that the big park has a frisbee golf course. It is like regular golf, but you throw a frisbee into metal baskets with chains. When it goes in, the chains go jingle. There are nine holes. Some are long and some go around trees. You count your throws, and fewer is better. I got a three on one hole, which dad said is called par. I got an eight on the hole with the big tree, because I hit the tree like four times. Dad beat me overall, but only by five. He said he has been practicing frisbee for thirty years and I have been practicing for one summer. That actually made me feel good. Lucas came too and kept the scorecard, and he wrote my eight sideways, which he says is the sign for like a zillion. I want to go back with Theo, because Theo is very competitive.
entries.highlight: Played frisbee golf for the first time at the big park with dad and counted his throws.

entries.title: Shark detective part two
entries.body: Kai came over and we built a blanket cave, like the old days, but now we are too big for the couch cushion kind. So we used the bunk bed and clipped blankets to it. Inside we finished part two of our comic, Finn the shark detective. In part two someone is stealing the sunken treasure, and it turns out to be an octopus who is collecting shiny things for her babies. So she's not really bad, she's just a mom. That was my idea. Kai said that's a twist. He made the octopus say, I'm armed and dangerous, eight times. We have sixteen pages now. Kai's mom is going to make copies at her office so we can give one to Mr. Okafor, even though he is not our teacher anymore.
entries.favorite: Finishing the comic in the blanket cave
entries.highlight: Finished part two of the shark detective comic with Kai inside a blanket cave.

entries.title: Biking the long trail with Sofia
entries.body: Sofia and me rode the long bike trail at the big park with our parents. It goes all the way around the lake, and it is four miles. Four! When I was seven, riding to the park was a big deal. There is a part that goes through a tunnel under the road, and when you yell in it, it echoes. We yelled our names and it said back Matthew, Matthew, Matthew. Sofia rides really fast down the hills. I am more careful, but I go faster up the hills. We stopped halfway and had water and granola bars. Sofia told me she found out she is in Ms. Chen's class for third grade. I don't know mine yet. I hope I am with her and Theo. The lake was so big I pretended it was the ocean and kept looking for fins. My legs are like jelly now.
entries.highlight: Rode the long bike trail with Sofia and their parents, the longest ride he had ever done.

entries.title: Lucas floated with no floaties
entries.body: Today Lucas floated on his back with NO floaties! We have been practicing all summer, me and him and Miss Marina. At the pool he said, Matty, watch, don't help. So I stood next to him but kept my hands up out of the water so he could see I wasn't touching. He laid back, tummy up to the sky, and he floated for like ten seconds. Ten whole seconds! Then he stood up and screamed I DID IT, just like when he caught the frisbee. I was so happy I hugged him and we both went under. Mom was crying a little, like at the movies. I remembered when I floated by myself for the first time and mom did a happy dance. Now Lucas has his own floating day. It feels even better than mine, somehow.
entries.highlight: Watched proudly as Lucas floated on his back without floaties for the first time after practicing together all summer.

entries.title: Last ice cream truck of summer
entries.body: I heard the ice cream truck music coming down the street, and I ran to get my wallet. I have my own money now from washing cars. My puppy fund is separate, I don't touch that. Lucas came running too, but he didn't have any money. So I bought his too. I got the shark popsicle with the gumball eyes. It is the same one I got when I was six, and it still tastes like blue. Lucas got the one shaped like a cartoon character, but the face melted in like two minutes and it looked creepy. We laughed so hard. Then we sat on the curb. Lucas said thank you for buying mine. I said, that's what big brothers do. It cost me three dollars, but it was worth it.
entries.highlight: Caught the ice cream truck one last time before school with Lucas and shared his money.

entries.title: Dad and me make lasagna
entries.body: Dad and me made lasagna tonight, which is the hardest thing I ever cooked. It has so many steps. First the sauce, with meat and tomatoes and garlic. Then the cheese part, with ricotta and an egg. Then you boil the big flat noodles, and they are slippery like seaweed. You do layers. Sauce, noodles, cheese, sauce, noodles, cheese, and so on. Dad let me do all the layers. I had to make sure the noodles didn't overlap too much. Then mozzarella on top. It baked for an hour and the whole house smelled amazing. Mom said, this is restaurant quality. I remember when I was six and I helped dad with mac and cheese and some fell on the floor. Now I make lasagna.
entries.highlight: Made a lasagna with dad from scratch, carefully building every layer.

entries.title: Taco night with grandma's salsa
entries.body: Grandma came over for taco night. She brought her homemade salsa with tomatoes from her garden. When I was six, I tried one tiny bit of salsa and drank my whole milk. Tonight I put a whole spoonful on my taco. It was a little spicy, but I didn't even need my milk. Okay, I took one sip. I still like the crunchy shells best, but I put lettuce on now. I used to say no lettuce. Grandma said my taste buds are growing up. Lucas still eats only cheese and shells. Grandma told him, you'll get there, look at your brother. Lucas said, I'm going to eat salsa when I'm eight. I said, I'll help you practice.
entries.highlight: Had a family taco night with grandma and tried her homemade salsa without needing milk.

entries.title: Dog walking day at the shelter
entries.body: The animal shelter had a dog walking day where families can come and walk the dogs. Mom said we could go, just to help. She said it twice, just to help. I walked a dog named Pepper. She was black and white and medium size and she pulled a little on the leash. I stopped walking every time she pulled, like the man at the park told me last winter. And it worked! By the end she walked next to me. The shelter lady said I was a natural. I asked if they have Pomeranians. She said sometimes, and they get adopted fast. I wanted to take Pepper home so bad. But I didn't ask, because mom said just to help. On the way home I asked mom, can we come back? She said yes.
entries.highlight: Helped walk dogs at the animal shelter's community walking day with mom.

entries.title: First day of third grade
entries.body: First day of third grade! Sofia is in my class again! We were in the same class in first grade with Ms. Rivera, and now we're together again. Theo is in the class next door, which I was kind of sad about, but we have the same recess. My teacher is Ms. Chen. She has a class aquarium with a real angelfish in it. I knew it was a good sign. I was a little nervous, because third grade is when you do multiplication and longer books. But Ms. Chen said we're going to read a whole novel together this year. A novel! I wore my shark tooth necklace for luck. I didn't really need it, but it's tradition. At lunch me and Sofia traded snacks like old times.
entries.highlight: Started third grade in Ms. Chen's class, was happy Sofia was there again, and felt only a little nervous.

entries.title: Lucas rode a pedal bike
entries.body: After school we went to the park, because Lucas got a pedal bike. A real one! He practiced on the balance bike since April, and now he's ready. I told him I would run next to him, like I did with the balance bike and like dad did with me. He said, don't let go. I said I won't. Then he started pedaling, and he was going straight, and I let go a little. He looked back and saw me behind him, and he yelled, you let go! But he kept riding! He rode all the way to the bench. He was so happy he forgot to be mad. I said, sorry, dad did the same trick on me. He said, it's a good trick. He's only four and he can ride a bike.
entries.highlight: Took Lucas to the park and helped him ride his new pedal bike for the first time.

entries.title: Sofia's reading tent
entries.body: Sofia came over on Saturday and we made a reading tent in the backyard, with the big sheet over the picnic table, like the one I made with Kai a long time ago. We got the same book from the library, a mystery about kids who find a secret map in a museum. We took turns reading the pages out loud. Sofia does really good voices for the old museum guard. I did the voice for the mean guy, all low and creepy. Laser was watching from the window. We read eight chapters! When we stopped, Sofia said she can't wait for Ms. Chen's novel. She said I read faster than her now. I said, you're the cartwheel teacher, I'm the reading guy. She laughed. It was a really cozy afternoon.
entries.highlight: Built a reading tent with Sofia and they took turns reading pages of the same book out loud.

entries.title: Asking to go back to the shelter
entries.body: I asked mom and dad if we can go back to the shelter. Mom said not this weekend, but soon. Then we had a family meeting at the kitchen table, all four of us. Dad got out the paper with my answers from the spring. He asked me the questions again, and my answers were the same. Mom asked, are you sure Laser would be okay with a dog? I said, I watched Laser with all the dogs through the window, and the lady at the park said her Pomeranian lives with two cats. Lucas said he would do the water bowl for the puppy too. Mom and dad looked at each other the way they did before Laser. I didn't say anything, because I didn't want to jinx it. But my heart was going so fast.
entries.favorite: Mom saying not this weekend, but soon
entries.highlight: Asked mom and dad to return to the shelter, and they had a serious family talk about a puppy.

entries.title: Meal prep Monday with dad
entries.body: Dad had an idea. On Monday nights we will make lunches for the whole week. Like a lunch factory. He chopped the vegetables and I made the sandwiches, and Lucas put crackers in the little containers. Then we put everything in the fridge with names on it. I made mine turkey and cheese, cut in triangles, because triangles still taste better. That is still a fact. I made Lucas's peanut butter and jelly with the crusts off, because he won't eat crusts. When I was in first grade I didn't even know how to pack a lunch. Now I am the sandwich manager. Dad said it saves so much time in the morning. I think it's also fun because we do it together.
entries.favorite: Making the lunch boxes like a factory
entries.highlight: Helped dad prepare a week of school lunches like an assembly line.

entries.title: Ruby and the summer journal results
entries.body: Ruby came over after dinner to finish our summer experiment. We put our nature journals side by side and looked at all the pond pages. In June there was the heron and tall water. In July there were the ducklings and the turtle and lower water. In August the ducklings were almost as big as their mom, and the lily pads had flowers. Ruby said that's called observation over time, and that's what real scientists do. I said, it's kind of like us. In first grade I was scared of the deep end and now I jump off the diving board. Ruby said, that's actually a really good point. She wrote it in her journal. Ruby never writes down my ideas, so that felt good.
entries.highlight: Compared summer nature journals with Ruby and talked about what they learned at the pond.

entries.title: Sprinkler after homework, third grade style
entries.body: It was so hot today, like ninety-one degrees, even though it's September. Before I could play, I had my first multiplication homework. The twos. Two times one is two, two times two is four. It's easy because it's like counting by twos. Ms. Chen says it gets harder with the sevens. Then mom turned on the sprinkler, the back and forth kind. Lucas asked if we could play sprinkler limbo, and I didn't even know he remembered that! He was only three. So we played, and we both still got wet every time and lost every time. Laser watched from the window like always, with her tail going back and forth. Some things stay the same, even in third grade.
entries.highlight: Finished his multiplication homework and then cooled off in the sprinkler with Lucas.

entries.title: Frisbee golf with Theo
entries.body: I finally took Theo to play frisbee golf at the big park. I told him he's very competitive, and he said, I am not, and then he wanted to keep score on his phone. He doesn't have a phone, it was his dad's phone. On the second hole he threw it from really far, and it went right in the basket, jingle! He yelled so loud a man on the next hole turned around. I got par on the hole with the big tree this time, which was my worst hole with dad. So I'm getting better. In the end Theo won by two. I said, nice one, and I meant it. He said, you are really good at the trees now. We played the whole thing again. It's harder now that we're in different classes, so it was nice to hang out. On the walk home we argued about great whites and hammerheads again, like always.
entries.highlight: Played frisbee golf with Theo, who turned out to be as competitive as expected.

entries.title: Neighborhood water fight
entries.body: In the afternoon it was still really hot, so me and Lucas started a water fight in the front yard. And then the kids next door came over with their squirt guns. And then the family across the street came. Even some of the grown ups! There were like fifteen people. I was on a team with Lucas and the neighbor girl, who is in first grade. I made sure Lucas and her didn't get blasted in the face, because they're little. Mr. Patel from down the street had a giant water cannon. We all teamed up against him. Mom made lemonade for everyone after. Dad said, we should do this every year. I agree. A lot of the neighbors said Lucas is so big now.
entries.highlight: Started a backyard water fight that turned into a neighborhood event on a hot September weekend.

entries.title: The shark documentary at the big theater
entries.body: We went to the special movie theater with the giant screen to watch a real shark documentary. It was so big it felt like we were in the water. There was a part with a whole school of hammerheads, like a hundred of them swimming together. Hammerheads really are the best, sorry Theo. They showed a diver swimming right next to a whale shark, which is the biggest shark in the world but it only eats tiny plankton. When I was six I said I would never swim in deep water like the aquarium. Now I think I want to be a diver like that someday. Lucas was scared during the great white part, so I whispered facts to him. Then he wasn't scared. Mom said I am her favorite tour guide.
entries.favorite: The hammerhead on the giant screen
entries.highlight: Saw a shark documentary at the big-screen theater with the family and felt amazed instead of scared.

entries.title: Last day at the outdoor pool
entries.body: Today was the last day of the outdoor pool before it closes for the year. We stayed for the whole afternoon. I jumped off the diving board like twenty times. I tried a pencil jump, where you go in straight like a pencil, and a cannonball, and a starfish. Did you know a real starfish doesn't even have blood? It uses sea water instead. Lucas said gross. Then I went to the shallow end and me and Lucas floated on our backs next to each other and looked at the clouds. One cloud looked like a puppy. Lucas said it looked like Laser. We argued, and then we decided it was both. When the lifeguard blew the last whistle of the summer, everybody clapped. I felt a little sad. This summer I jumped off the diving board, and Lucas floated, and we both got braver. Summer always ends too fast.
entries.highlight: Spent the last day of the outdoor pool season swimming, diving and floating with Lucas.

entries.title: Labor Day rematch with dad
entries.body: It's Labor Day, no school. Dad said, remember Father's Day? I said I promised I'd get you back. So it was a rematch. Dad versus me and Lucas. Mom said she is the referee this time. Dad had a whole bucket hidden behind the shed! I saw it, though, because I noticed the water on the grass. Detective skills, like Rex. So I told Lucas to distract him again, the same trick, and he did. And this time I grabbed the bucket before dad could. Dad got soaked AGAIN. Mom said the boys win, and dad fell on the grass and said, I've been outsmarted by my own sons. Lucas jumped on his tummy. It was the last big water fight of summer, and it was a great one.
entries.highlight: Had a Labor Day water fight rematch against dad, who had promised revenge since Father's Day.

entries.title: Trying the swim team practice
entries.body: Coach Ray said I'm ready to try the beginner swim team, so today was my first practice at the indoor pool. It's harder than lessons. We had to swim whole laps, all the way down and back. The pool is twenty-five yards. I swam a whole lap of freestyle without stopping, reaching and pulling and turning my head to breathe like I learned last fall. At the end I was so tired I had to hang on the wall for a long time. A girl next to me said, that was good for your first day. Then we practiced kicking with boards for like fifteen minutes. Coach Ray yells encouraging things, like, legs legs legs! He said it like a hundred times. I don't know if I want to do swim team for real yet. But I want to keep trying. On the way home I asked mom, did you know a sailfish can swim faster than a car on the highway? She said, so that's your next goal? I said, very funny.
entries.favorite: Swimming a whole lap of freestyle
entries.highlight: Tried a beginner swim team practice at the indoor pool and swam a full lap of freestyle.

entries.title: Bottomless pit after swim practice
entries.body: After swim practice I was more hungry than I have ever been in my whole life. When I was seven I said swimming makes you hungry. Swim team makes you twice as hungry. Mom made spaghetti and meatballs. I ate a whole plate, and then another whole plate, and then garlic bread, and a pear. Lucas watched me with his mouth open. He said, are you a bottomless pit? He remembered that! I said yes, still. Dad said Coach Ray told him swimmers burn a lot of energy, so it's okay. I did the long noodle slurp, and it hit my nose and made a sauce mustache, like when I was little. Lucas did it too. Mom said, still a slurping family. I fell asleep at eight o'clock.
entries.highlight: Was extremely hungry after his first swim team practice and ate two plates of spaghetti.

entries.title: Multiplication war at game night
entries.body: Ms. Chen told us about a card game to practice multiplication, so we played it at family game night. It's like the war card game, but you each flip a card and multiply them, and whoever says the answer first wins both cards. I was really fast at the twos and fives and tens. The sevens are still hard. Seven times eight, I always forget. It's fifty-six. Dad let me win at first and I could tell, so I said, dad, play for real. Then he played for real and I still won some! Lucas played the adding version with mom, where you just add the two cards. He counted on his fingers. Laser stole the queen of hearts and ran under the couch. We played with fifty-one cards after that.
entries.highlight: Played a multiplication card game at family game night that Ms. Chen suggested.

entries.title: Getting Lucas his first library card
entries.body: Today Lucas got his very own library card! He is almost five, and mom said he can have one now. I came too, because I remember getting mine with mom in second grade. Lucas had to sign his name on the back. He can write L-U-C-A-S now, but the S was backwards. The librarian said it still counts. Then I showed him where the dinosaur books are, and the picture books, and the comfy reading bean bags. He picked out five dinosaur books and one about a cat that looks like Laser. I helped him carry them to the desk, and the librarian scanned his card, beep, and he looked so proud. On the way home I read him the cat book in the car. He said, when I'm big I want to read chapter books like you.
entries.highlight: Took Lucas to the library with mom to get Lucas his first library card.

entries.title: Indoor pool Sunday with Lucas
entries.body: Now that the outdoor pool is closed, we go to the indoor pool on Sundays. It's warm inside and smells like chlorine, and it's loud because of the echo. Lucas swam from the steps to me with no floaties, like he does now. Then he wanted to race. I said okay, but I'll only use my legs. We raced from one rope to the other. I let him get ahead and then I tied him at the end. He said, I almost beat you! I said, you almost did. Then I did a few laps in the lap lane to practice for swim team. The lifeguard said my freestyle looks good. When I was six, the indoor pool was where I stayed in the shallow part with floaties at my birthday party. Now it feels like my second home.
entries.highlight: Spent Sunday at the indoor pool helping Lucas swim and playing a short race.

entries.title: Teaching the leg catch at recess
entries.body: I brought my frisbee to recess again, and kids from both third grade classes came to play, including Theo. Everyone wanted to learn the leg catch I showed Theo in June. So I was the teacher. I lined everybody up and I threw it slow, one at a time. I told them, lift your leg, watch it the whole time, and don't be scared of it. Most people got hit in the knee at first, just like me. Sofia got it on her fourth try and did a cartwheel to celebrate. A boy named Caleb got it too, the one I picked for kickball last year. Ms. Chen watched and said, you're a patient coach, Matthew. I said, I learned from my dad. And from teaching Lucas everything.
entries.favorite: The whole group trying the trick
entries.highlight: Taught a group of third graders the frisbee leg catch at recess.

entries.title: Grandma's rematch at the mystery game
entries.body: Grandma came for family game night, and she said, I want a rematch at the mystery game. Last time I won and she said I have a detective brain. Now I've read all four dog detective books and two other mystery books, so I had even more practice. I kept my notes really neat this time in a little grid, like the detectives do. After four turns I knew it was the cook, in the ballroom, with the candlestick. Grandma said, how did you do that so fast? I said, process of elimination. Dad's mouth fell open. He said, where did you learn that phrase? I said, from Rex. Grandma laughed so hard. She said she is never playing that game with me again. Then she asked to play again.
entries.highlight: Played the mystery board game with grandma again at family game night and solved it fast.

entries.title: Frisbee golf with dad and Lucas
entries.body: We went to frisbee golf again on Sunday, and this time Lucas came too. He's too small to throw from where we throw, so I made him his own little spot closer to the basket on every hole. I gave him my old frisbee, the soft one. On the fourth hole he threw it and it hit the pole and fell into the basket. Jingle! He jumped up and down and said, did you hear it? I said I heard it! Dad and me still kept our scores. I beat dad on three holes, including the big tree hole. Overall dad beat me by just two now. In August it was five. I'm getting closer. I told dad, by next summer I'm going to beat you. He said, I believe it.
entries.highlight: Played frisbee golf with dad and Lucas, helping Lucas get his first frisbee into a basket.

entries.title: Theo and me after school
entries.body: Me and Theo met at the park after school. It's weird not being in the same class. We were together in first grade and second grade. Now I only see him at recess and lunch. We sat on top of the climbing dome and he told me about his class. They have a class pet too, a lizard named Spike. And his teacher reads them a book every afternoon, like Mr. Okafor did with the lighthouse book. I told him about Ms. Chen's class aquarium and our novel. Theo said he sometimes feels kind of alone at lunch on Tuesdays because I have reading club. I didn't know that. So I said, let's sit together every other day at least. He said okay. Then we played shark tag on the dome until the streetlights came on.
entries.highlight: Met Theo at the park after school and talked about being in different classes for the first time.

entries.title: Back to the shelter to walk dogs
entries.body: Mom kept her promise, and we went back to the animal shelter for another dog walking afternoon. I looked for Pepper, the dog I walked in August. The shelter lady told me Pepper got adopted by a family with a big yard! I felt happy and a tiny bit sad at the same time, because I really liked her. Mom said that's a happy kind of sad. Today I walked a big old dog named Bruno. He was slow and gray around his nose. He didn't pull at all. He just sniffed every single flower. I didn't rush him. The shelter lady said older dogs need patient people. I asked again if they had a Pomeranian. She said not today, but they come in sometimes, and she wrote my name on a little card.
entries.highlight: Returned to the shelter's family dog walk and found out the dog he walked before had been adopted.

entries.title: The first leaf pile of fall
entries.body: The leaves are starting to fall again, so me and Lucas went to the park and made a leaf pile under the big tree, the same tree where Noah and me made one last year. Lucas used his whole body to push leaves, like a little bulldozer. It got almost as tall as him. Then he wanted to jump in from the bench. I checked first to make sure there were no sticks or rocks in the pile, because I'm the big brother and that's my job. Then I said, okay, go. He jumped, and leaves flew everywhere, and he came up with a leaf stuck on his nose. We did it over and over. Then we found a worm, and Lucas wanted to name it Steve, too! I told him Noah already named a worm Steve. He said, this is Steve Two.
entries.favorite: Lucas jumping in from the bench
entries.highlight: Made the first leaf pile of fall at the park with Lucas, the way he once did with Noah.

entries.title: Rainy day and the class novel
entries.body: It rained all day, so we had indoor recess again. Some kids played board games, but me and Sofia read our class novel by the window. It's about a boy and his dog who get lost in the mountains, and they have to survive by themselves. We're on chapter nine. Ms. Chen let us read ahead if we promise not to spoil it. In this chapter the dog finds water when the boy is too tired to look. Sofia said, I think the dog is smarter than the boy. I said, dogs are smarter than people think. I said, did you know some dolphins have helped lost swimmers get back to shore? I read that in my ocean book. Then I thought about Waffles, and if Waffles would find me in the mountains. Probably. Ms. Chen read the next chapter out loud by the window while the rain hit the glass. It felt like the perfect day for that book.
entries.favorite: Ms. Chen reading by the window
entries.highlight: Spent a rainy indoor recess reading ahead in the class novel and talking about it with Sofia.

entries.title: Theo and the lunch table plan
entries.body: After school I met Theo at the park again. We've been sitting together at lunch every other day, like we planned. Theo said Tuesdays are better now, because on Tuesdays he sits with a boy from his class who also likes sharks. So I helped kind of, by asking him about it. I felt good about that. Then we played on the zip line and tried to see who could hold on longest with no feet. Theo won, but my hands were sore from swim practice. I told him about Laser knocking over my cup, and he laughed. Then I told him about the shelter list with my name on it. He said, if you get a Pomeranian, can I meet it first? I said, after me and Lucas. He said fair.
entries.favorite: Theo saying Tuesdays are better now
entries.highlight: Played at the park with Theo, who said sitting together at lunch had helped.

entries.title: Recess buddy for a new kid
entries.body: There was a new kid in our class today. His name is Ezra, and he moved here from another state. Ms. Chen asked who wants to be his recess buddy, and I raised my hand fast. I remember how my tummy felt on the first day of second grade when I didn't know where to put my lunch. So I showed him everything. The best swing, the one that goes the highest. The tube slide where I used to hide in first grade. The spot by the fence where we play shark tag. I explained the rules, and he played, and he was the last minnow! Sofia said, he's fast like me. At the end Ezra said thanks. I said, you can sit with us at lunch tomorrow. He smiled for the first time today.
entries.favorite: Showing the new kid the best swing
entries.highlight: Volunteered to be a recess buddy for a new student and showed him around the playground.

entries.title: Fall car wash and leaf cleanup
entries.body: Dad and me washed the car in the driveway, maybe for the last time before it gets too cold. The water from the hose was so cold my fingers turned red. But we did it fast. There were leaves stuck everywhere, in the windshield wipers and in the little crack by the trunk. Inside the car there were also crackers, Lucas's sock, and a dinosaur under the seat. Dad said, our car is a museum. I vacuumed the inside with the little vacuum while dad did the windows. Dad said I am faster than him now. He gave me five dollars and I put it right in my puppy fund. It has twenty-six dollars now. That's enough for a collar and a leash. I keep counting it like it's going to change.
entries.highlight: Washed the car with dad on a cool fall afternoon and cleaned out the leaves stuck everywhere.

entries.title: Sofia and the novel ending
entries.body: Me and Sofia both finished the class novel, so we went to the park to talk about it, like a book club with swings. In the ending, the boy and his dog get found by a ranger, because the dog barks at the helicopter. We both cried a little bit when we read it, even though it was a happy ending. Sofia said she cried at the part where the boy gives the dog the last of his food. I said I cried at the part where the boy says, you saved me. That's what Lucas said to me when I checked his closet for monsters. I didn't tell Sofia that part, but I thought it. Then Sofia did ten cartwheels in a row, and I did three. My cartwheels are good now. She taught me in first grade.
entries.favorite: Talking about the ending on the swings
entries.highlight: Talked about the ending of the class novel with Sofia at the park after they both finished it.

entries.title: Making apple chips with mom
entries.body: Mom and me went apple picking again last weekend, so we had too many apples. Mom said, let's make apple chips. I sliced them really thin with the slicer, very carefully because it's sharp, and mom watched. Then we laid them on the pan in rows, sprinkled cinnamon on them, and baked them for a really long time at a low temperature. The house smelled like the orchard donuts. When they came out, they were curly and crispy. I ate like twenty right away. Lucas said they are like apple potato chips. I packed some in my lunch for tomorrow in my lunch factory container. I'm going to trade some to Ruby for mango, because she said she wants to try them. Some trades never change.
entries.highlight: Made homemade cinnamon apple chips with mom using apples from the orchard.

entries.title: Mom and dad said we can go look
entries.body: Tonight at dinner mom and dad said they have news. Dad said, we've been watching how you take care of Laser for a year and a half. And how you helped Lucas with his water bowl job, and how you were at the shelter with Pepper and Bruno. Then mom said, so we decided we can go to the shelter and look at puppies. Just to look. Soon. I didn't scream. I wanted to, but I just sat there with my fork in the air. Then I said, really? And mom said really. Lucas screamed for me. Then I ran and got my puppy fund jar and put it on the table. Twenty-six dollars. Dad said, put that away, but he was smiling. Two years ago I asked every week, and they said we will see. Now we will see is almost here.
entries.favorite: The words we can go look
entries.highlight: Heard from mom and dad that the family could visit the shelter to look at puppies after a careful decision.

entries.title: Mom and me in the lazy river
entries.body: Later at the water park, me and mom floated on the lazy river in a double tube while dad took Lucas to the splash zone. It goes so slow, so you can just talk. Mom said, do you remember the water park two summers ago? I said yes, I wore a life jacket and I skipped the steep slide. She said, and today you went down it three times. Then she said she is proud of me, but not just for the slide. She said she is proud of how I help Lucas, and how I was a recess buddy for Ezra, and how I'm patient with Laser. I didn't know she knew about Ezra. Ms. Chen told her! I felt my face get warm. We floated around the river two more times without talking much. It was nice. Just mom and me.
entries.favorite: Talking to mom in the lazy river
entries.highlight: Floated in the lazy river with mom at the indoor water park and talked about how much he has changed.

entries.title: Ezra's first shark tag win
entries.body: At recess we played shark tag, which is still my game from second grade. Now Ezra plays with us every day. Today Ezra was the shark and he tagged everybody, even Sofia, who never gets tagged. He was so happy. He told me that at his old school he didn't really have a group. I said, well now you do. Theo came over from his class too, and Ezra and Theo found out they both like the same shark cartoon, so now they talk about that. I like when my friends become friends with each other. Ms. Chen said our recess group is like a little school of minnows. I said, a school of hammerheads. Ezra said, what's a hammerhead? So I spent the rest of recess explaining, starting with, did you know sharks are older than dinosaurs? He thinks they're the coolest now too.
entries.favorite: Ezra being the shark this time
entries.highlight: Played shark tag at recess with Ezra, who now plays with the group every day.

entries.title: Making a puppy shopping list with mom
entries.body: Thursday was mom and me time. We made a list, even though we haven't even been to the shelter yet. Mom said, it's good to be prepared, but remember, just looking. The list says: a collar, a leash, a food bowl and a water bowl, puppy food, a crate, a bed, chew toys so he doesn't chew my stuff, a brush, especially if it's a Pomeranian, and poop bags. Lots of poop bags. I wrote Waffles at the top, and mom said, what if the puppy already has a name? I didn't think about that. I said, then we can ask the puppy what it wants. She laughed. Then I said, no, really, I think Waffles is still the name. I've had that name since I was six. That's like half my life of waiting.
entries.highlight: Spent his Thursday time with mom making a careful list of supplies a puppy would need.

entries.title: Making my shark costume
entries.body: This morning me and mom finished my Halloween costume. I wanted to make it myself this year, not buy it. It's a gray hoodie, and we made the hammerhead part out of cardboard covered in gray felt, sticking out on both sides of the hood. The eyes go on the very ends, because that's where real hammerheads have their eyes. Did you know their wide heads help them find stingrays hiding in the sand? I explained that to mom while she glued. I cut out white felt teeth, like twenty of them, and mom helped with the hot glue. Last year I was a scuba diver with soda bottle tanks, and Lucas was a clownfish. This year Lucas wanted to be a dinosaur, so he is, a green one with spikes. I helped him put his tail on with safety pins. He kept chasing me around saying, dinosaurs eat sharks. I said that's not even scientifically possible, they lived at different times. He didn't care.
entries.highlight: Spent Halloween morning finishing his homemade hammerhead shark costume with mom.

entries.title: Laser and the candy wrappers
entries.body: The day after Halloween, me and Lucas were eating our two pieces of candy, and we put the wrappers in a pile on the floor. Laser found them. She loves crinkly sounds. She batted one across the floor, and then she ran and slid right into the whole pile, and they went flying everywhere like confetti. Then she rolled on her back in them. Lucas said Laser is having her own Halloween. I picked up the wrappers fast, though, because Ruby told me some candy is bad for cats, especially chocolate. I gave Laser a crinkle ball toy instead, so she could keep the sound without the danger. She played with it until her nine o'clock zoomies, and then she did both at the same time. I think she is the silliest cat in the whole world.
entries.highlight: Watched Laser play in a pile of crinkly Halloween candy wrappers the day after trick-or-treating.

entries.title: The shelter called
entries.body: Today when I got home from school, mom said, the shelter called. My heart stopped. She said the lady remembered my name on the little card, and she said a Pomeranian puppy might be coming in next week, from a family who couldn't keep it. I asked, can we go tomorrow? Mom said no, the puppy isn't there yet, and we have to wait for them to check that it's healthy. So now I have to wait more. I have waited two whole years, so I thought waiting would be easy now. But it's actually harder, because now it's so close. I told Laser all about it. She yawned. Lucas said, I'm going to teach it to roar. Dad said, let's not get ahead of ourselves, buddy. But dad was smiling again.
entries.favorite: Hearing my name on the phone
entries.highlight: Heard that the shelter called his mom about a Pomeranian puppy coming in soon.

entries.title: Practicing with a neighbor's leash
entries.body: At the park after school I saw our neighbor, Mr. Patel, walking his two dogs. I told him about the shelter, and he said, want to practice? He let me hold both leashes! Two dogs at once is way harder than one. They want to go in different directions, and one wanted to sniff a tree and one wanted to chase a squirrel. I remembered to stop walking when they pulled. It took a while, but they figured it out. Mr. Patel said I was a pro already. I told him I've been doing puppy research since I was six. That's when I made the poster with four reasons. Mom still has it in the closet. I think she kept it because she knew this day would come. Or maybe she just keeps everything.
entries.highlight: Practiced walking dogs at the park with a neighbor and showed how much he had learned.

entries.title: Lucas and me get the room ready
entries.body: Lucas asked if the puppy will sleep in his room or mine. I said, there might not even be a puppy yet, we are just looking. But he really wanted to get ready. So we found a good spot in the corner of the living room by the window, where the sun comes in, and where Laser can see it but also get away. I explained that to Lucas, that Laser needs her own space so she doesn't get scared. He nodded like a grown up. Then he put his old dinosaur in the spot and said, this is for the puppy to have a friend. That was really sweet. I used to think Lucas was annoying when he knocked over my towers. Now he's my partner. Waffles is going to have two brothers.
entries.favorite: Lucas putting his dinosaur in the puppy bed
entries.highlight: Helped Lucas pick a spot for a possible puppy bed, explaining it might not happen yet.

entries.title: Field trip to the aquarium
entries.body: Today our class went on a field trip to the aquarium! The same one where me and mom went when I was six. I remember I said the big tank was so deep that I would never swim in it. Now I swim laps on the swim team. When we walked through the shark tunnel, everybody was looking up, and I started telling Ezra and Sofia facts, like I always do. Did you know hammerheads can see almost all the way around? And sharks keep growing new teeth, like a thousand in their whole life. Sofia said, you say did you know like a hundred times a day. I said, did you know that's because there are so many facts? She laughed. Then the aquarium guide asked a question about sharks, and I answered it. She said, you know a lot! Ms. Chen said Matthew is our class shark expert. We also saw a giant octopus, and I thought about the documentary. The big tank isn't scary anymore. It's beautiful.
entries.favorite: Being the tour guide in the shark tunnel
entries.highlight: Went to the aquarium on a third-grade field trip and shared shark facts with his class in the tunnel.

entries.title: Telling Theo about the puppy
entries.body: After the shelter I was too excited to stay home, so dad took me to meet Theo at the park before dark. I told him everything. The orange fur, the tiny tongue, the hand lick, and mom saying maybe. Theo said, maybe from your mom is basically yes. I said, that's what I said! We ran around the whole playground screaming, and an old man on the bench laughed at us. Then we sat on top of the climbing dome and I told Theo, you know, I used to ask for a puppy every single week. Every single week since first grade. Theo said, I know, I was there. You talked about Waffles at like every recess. He said, if it happens, I still get to meet it right after you and Lucas. I said deal. Then it got cold and dark, and we went home. It was the best day ever. Again. Twice in one day.
entries.favorite: Theo running around the playground with me
entries.highlight: Met Theo at the park in the evening and told him all about the Pomeranian puppy and mom's maybe.

entries.title: First snow
entries.body: It snowed! It was not a lot but we still went sledding down the little hill after school. There was barely enough snow to cover the grass, and you could see green parts sticking through. Lucas went down on his tummy, headfirst, like a penguin, just like I used to do. I said, Lucas, that's my move! He said, now it's my move too. The sled went kind of slow because there wasn't much snow, but we still went down like fifteen times. My cheeks got really cold and then we had hot chocolate. I put in the tiny marshmallows, like a hundred, which is still the right number. Tomorrow we go to the shelter just to look. I can't stop thinking about it. I don't know how I am going to sleep tonight.
entries.highlight: Went sledding on the first light snow of the season with Lucas and had hot chocolate afterwards.

entries.title: Halloween
entries.body: I was a shark for Halloween and Lucas was a dinosaur. My shark costume has a fin on the hood and felt teeth around my face. It's a hammerhead, obviously, but people kept saying great white, and I kept explaining. We got so much candy. We went to every house on our street and the next street, and I held Lucas's hand at the scary house with the fog machine, just like last year. He was braver this year, though. He roared at the skeleton. At home we dumped everything on the floor. I traded my raisins for Lucas's chocolate. Four raisin boxes for four chocolates, which is fair, because he actually likes raisins. Laser was scared of the doorbell. Every time it rang she ran under the couch. So I gave her a treat each time, and by the end she only hid halfway.
entries.highlight: Went trick-or-treating as a shark with Lucas the dinosaur, traded candy, and noticed Laser was scared of the doorbell.

entries.title: Purple ice cream on a waffle
entries.body: We went to the ice cream shop with my whole family on Sunday. They had a new flavor that was purple. The man said it is ube, which is a purple yam. A purple yam! I didn't know there was such a thing. I tried a little taste on the tiny spoon, and it tasted like vanilla and a little bit like a cookie. So I got purple ice cream on a waffle. A waffle cone, but they put a whole little waffle under it like a plate. Dad said, a waffle for the future owner of Waffles. Everybody laughed. Lucas got sprinkles everywhere, on the table, on his shirt, in his hair, and somehow on mom's shoe. I ate the whole thing, even the waffle. I had no tummy ache.
entries.highlight: Went to the ice cream shop with the whole family and ate purple ice cream on a waffle cone while Lucas got sprinkles everywhere.

entries.title: Laser knocked over my cup
entries.body: Laser is my kitten. Well, she is not really a kitten anymore, but she is still my kitten. She knocked my water cup off the table and then ran away really fast, like a gray laser beam. She did not even look back. She just looked at me first, with her paw on the cup, like she was asking permission, and then she pushed it anyway. The water went all over the floor and on my socks. Lucas laughed so hard he fell off his chair. Lucas is my little brother and he is four. I got a towel and cleaned it up, because that is part of having a cat. Then I tried to draw Laser, sitting on the windowsill like nothing happened. But cats are hard to draw. They still are, even with the shape trick.
entries.highlight: Laser knocked his water cup off the table and ran off, Lucas laughed, and he tried to draw her.

entries.title: We met a puppy!
entries.body: We went to the animal shelter just to look and there was a Pomeranian puppy. It was small and orange and fluffy, like a dandelion with legs, just like the one at the park in the summer. The shelter lady let us go in a little room with it. I sat on the floor very still, like I learned with Laser, so I wouldn't scare it. And it walked right up to me. It licked my hand. Its tongue was so tiny. Lucas sat next to me and used gentle hands with one finger, like I taught him with Laser. Mom watched for a long time. Then she said maybe. Maybe means almost yes. Dad squeezed my shoulder. I have been waiting since I was six. This is the best day ever.
entries.highlight: Visited the animal shelter just to look, met a Pomeranian puppy that licked his hand, and mom said maybe.

entries.title: Movie theater day
entries.body: It rained so we went to the movie theater. It rained so hard that we had to run from the car to the door and we were still soaked. We saw a wizard movie about a girl who finds out her cat can talk. Laser would never talk. She would just knock things over. I got popcorn and gummy worms. More gummy worms. I mixed them in the popcorn, which is my new invention, and dad tried it and said it was weird but good. In the movie the girl had a dog too, a little fluffy one that came everywhere with her, even to wizard school. I wish my puppy could come to the movies, but I do not have a puppy yet. Yet.
entries.highlight: Went to the movie theater on a rainy Sunday, saw a wizard movie, and wished his future puppy could come along.

entries.title: Indoor water park
entries.body: We went to the indoor water park. There was a wave pool and a really steep slide. In the summer I was one inch too short for the steep slide at the other water park. Today I stood at the height line and I was taller! I grew. I was a little scared but I went down anyway and it was so fast. You cross your arms and your legs and then the floor kind of drops and you go whoosh, and my stomach went up into my throat. At the bottom the water splashed so hard it went up my nose. I came up laughing. Then I did it two more times. The water was just lukewarm, not cold and not warm. After we got popsicles. Mine was cherry. I said that was the bravest thing since the diving board.
entries.highlight: Went to an indoor water park, was nervous about the steep slide but rode it anyway, then had popsicles.
